abstract: ArXiv:2610.19691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Subspace-design codes form a central unifying framework in coding theory, connecting probabilistic existence results and explicit algebraically structured constructions. The two core families are folded Reed-Solomon codes and univariate multiplicity codes, both possessing the subspace-design property. These codes reach list-decoding capacity with polynomial-size lists, but their alphabet size grows with code length and hurts practical efficiency. Goyal, Guruswami, and Hsieh achieved a major breakthrough: they constructed the first explicit subspace-design codes over constant-size alphabets via the Alon-Edmonds-Luby expander framework, settling an open problem and showing subspace-design properties can hold without large alphabets. Despite recent progress, constructing subspace-design codes with low-complexity efficient encoding remains a critical open challenge. This work gives an explicit construction of r-dimensional subspace-design codes over a constant alphabet whose size grows exponentially with r. By comparison, Goyal et al. (FOCS 2026) built r-dimensional subspace-design codes with alphabet size doubly exponential in r squared. Our construction is computationally efficient: encoding scales quadratically with block length and linearly with dimension r in field operations. We use modified algebraic geometry codes, replacing rational evaluation points with higher-degree places to obtain a valid additive code. To confirm parameter bounds, we use Moore matrices to analyze determinants with many zero entries. We also generalize univariate multiplicity codes, originally built from Reed-Solomon codes, to algebraic geometry codes, and prove these AG-multiplicity codes achieve optimal parameters.
tldr: The paper gives an efficient explicit construction of r-dimensional subspace-design codes over a constant alphabet whose size grows exponentially with r, using modified algebraic geometry codes and AG-multiplicity codes.
motivation: Subspace-design codes are a central framework in coding theory, but existing explicit constructions either have alphabet size growing with code length or, in the recent constant-alphabet breakthrough, suffer from doubly exponential alphabet size and high encoding complexity.
method: The construction replaces rational evaluation points in algebraic geometry codes with higher-degree places to obtain an additive code, and uses Moore matrices to analyze determinants with many zero entries; it also generalizes univariate multiplicity codes to algebraic geometry codes.
result: The new codes achieve an alphabet size exponential in r (improving over doubly exponential in r^2), with encoding time quadratic in block length and linear in r, and the AG-multiplicity codes are proven to achieve optimal parameters.
conclusion: This work significantly advances the efficient construction of subspace-design codes over small alphabets, making them more practical while maintaining the subspace-design property and list-decoding capacity.

title: Quantum-Resilient Secure Protocol For Decentralized Edge-IoT Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading Systems
authors: Ali Shahidinejad, Jamshid Aghaei, Mahdi Jalili
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rise of quantum computing presents substantial challenges to the security of Peer-to-Peer (P2P) energy trading systems. This paper introduces an innovative mutual authenticated session key agreement protocol aimed at protecting edge-IoT P2P energy trading communications in the quantum era. Each peer is an IoT-enabled smart metering device that is registered by an edge registration authority and acts as both producer and consumer. The proposed protocol incorporates CRYSTALS-Kyber's quantum-resistant cryptographic suite to guarantee the authenticity and confidentiality of negotiated session keys in the presence of quantum threats. Furthermore, it leverages the Hedera Hashgraph public blockchain, which is recognized for its quantum-resilient design, to ensure transparency and support efficient revocation mechanisms. Extensive comparative analyses have been conducted to demonstrate the protocol's superiority over existing alternatives, including both traditional schemes based on classical cryptography and emerging early-stage post-quantum approaches, in terms of performance and security features. By combining robust security and high efficiency, the proposed protocol fosters the development of resilient decentralized energy markets, paving the way for secure and sustainable energy distribution in the future.
tldr: The paper proposes a mutually authenticated session-key agreement protocol using CRYSTALS-Kyber and the Hedera Hashgraph blockchain to secure peer-to-peer energy trading among edge-IoT smart meters in a post-quantum era.
motivation: Quantum computers threaten the classical cryptography underpinning decentralized P2P energy trading among IoT smart-metering devices, motivating quantum-resistant authentication and key agreement for edge-IoT networks.
method: A mutual authentication and session-key agreement protocol is designed around the CRYSTALS-Kyber lattice-based KEM, combined with the Hedera Hashgraph public blockchain for transparency and efficient key revocation, then compared against classical and early post-quantum schemes on performance and security features.
result: Comparative analyses claim superior performance and richer security features relative to existing classical and early-stage post-quantum alternatives, including efficient revocation via the hashgraph ledger.
conclusion: The protocol is positioned as a practical, efficient security layer enabling resilient decentralized energy markets, though the contribution is systems-engineering oriented rather than an information-theoretic advance.

title: A Quantum-assisted Latent Surrogate Model For Bayesian Inversion Of Heterogeneous Material Properties On Nisq Hardware
authors: Dewangga Alfarisy, Catherine F. Higham, Eky Febrianto
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bayesian inversion is widely used in engineering applications, including material characterisation, structural damage identification, and medical diagnostics. These inverse problems are typically ill-posed, because localised variations in material properties must be inferred from noisy observations, and they are computationally intensive, since they often require many evaluations of a high-fidelity forward solver. Quantum computing has recently attracted considerable interest, partly because some near-term algorithms are feasible on NISQ hardware. In particular, PQC combined with classical optimisation enable a hybrid quantum-classical surrogate model. A central obstacle to applying such circuits to inversion is that the discretised parameter and response fields are far too high-dimensional to be embedded in a near-term quantum register. In this work we propose a quantum-assisted latent surrogate model for the Bayesian inversion of inhomogeneous material properties, in which latent compression bridges these high-dimensional fields and the small registers accessible to near-term circuits. The low intrinsic dimensional structure of the spatially varying conductivity and potential fields is exploited by reducing the conductivity through PCA and the response through a convolutional autoencoder. A PQC is then trained to map the latent conductivity to the latent response, and stochastic variational inference is performed entirely in latent space. The methodology is demonstrated on one- and two-dimensional inverse problems under both informative and non-informative priors. We further evaluate the model on IonQ simulator and Rigetti Cepheus-1-108Q, and use a lightweight learned denoising stage that recovers the noiseless accuracy to within a small residual. (The abstract has been shortened to meet arXiv's 1,920-character limit. For the full Abstract, please download the full Article.).
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical latent surrogate model uses parameterized quantum circuits and latent compression for Bayesian inversion of heterogeneous material properties on NISQ hardware.
motivation: Bayesian inversion for material characterization is computationally intensive and high-dimensional, making direct embedding in near-term quantum registers infeasible.
method: PCA compresses conductivity fields and a convolutional autoencoder compresses response fields; a PQC maps latent conductivity to latent response, with stochastic variational inference performed entirely in latent space and a learned denoising stage for hardware noise.
result: The approach is demonstrated on one- and two-dimensional inverse problems under informative and non-informative priors, and evaluated on IonQ simulator and Rigetti Cepheus-1-108Q, where denoising recovers noiseless accuracy to within a small residual.
conclusion: Latent compression bridges high-dimensional engineering fields and small quantum registers, enabling a near-term quantum-assisted surrogate for Bayesian inversion, but the work is an applied quantum machine learning contribution outside the core research directions.

title: Post-Optimization Subspace Corrections To Quantum Ans\"atze
authors: Prince Frederick Kwao, Bharath Sambasivam, Jason Saroni, Srivathsan Poyyapakkam Sundar, Edwin Barnes, Ayush Asthana
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Circuit depth and measurement count are the main limitations for chemical applications of the leading variational quantum algorithms on quantum computers. We show that both resource requirements can be reduced by augmenting adaptive variational quantum algorithms with post-optimization corrective techniques. We focus on two such techniques---Hamiltonian-moment Krylov subspace diagonalization and the identity-augmented quantum self-consistent equation of motion (q-sc-EOM)---applied to optimized ADAPT-VQE states without further ansatz growth or nonlinear optimization. Across molecular systems studied with up to 20 qubits, first-order Krylov correction reduces the optimized iterations (and the corresponding number of adaptive layers) needed to reach the [MATH] threshold by up to approximately sixfold, with a general trend toward larger reductions at higher determinant R\'enyi entropy. We also find measurement-cost reductions of up to approximately fortyfold using a suitable resource-cost model. Identity-augmented q-sc-EOM improves molecular potential-energy curves obtained from truncated ADAPT-VQE ans\"atze with limited expressivity and recovers accuracy from states produced by sampled operator ranking without additional gradient-based operator selection, providing an advantage when small pool gradients make selection measurement intensive. Together, these post-optimization corrections offer routes to improve energy accuracy and reduce adaptive circuit growth in quantum algorithms as quantum hardware advances.
tldr: Post-optimization subspace corrections to adaptive variational quantum eigensolver ansätze reduce circuit depth and measurement count for molecular simulations.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms for quantum chemistry are limited by circuit depth and measurement cost, requiring more efficient use of existing optimized states.
method: The authors augment optimized ADAPT-VQE states with Hamiltonian-moment Krylov subspace diagonalization and identity-augmented quantum self-consistent equation of motion (q-sc-EOM) without further ansatz growth or nonlinear optimization.
result: First-order Krylov correction reduces optimized iterations by up to about sixfold and measurement cost by up to about fortyfold, while identity-augmented q-sc-EOM improves molecular potential-energy curves from truncated ansätze.
conclusion: Post-optimization corrections offer practical routes to improve energy accuracy and reduce adaptive circuit growth in near-term quantum chemistry algorithms.

title: Shot- And Noise-Aware Pauli Correlation Encoding For Max-Cut Experiments On Ibm Heron Quantum Processor
authors: Achraf Boussahi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pauli correlation encoding (PCE) encodes [MATH] binary variables in the signs of [MATH]-body Pauli correlators of [MATH] qubits, and trains a parameterized circuit on a relaxed loss of sharpness [MATH]. The strongest published schedules sharpen this loss aggressively and are benchmarked with exact expectation values, whereas a quantum computer estimates correlators from a finite number of shots. We show that the sharpness is a hidden shot budget. Since the expected sign of a correlator estimated from [MATH] shots, [MATH], agrees with [MATH] to within [MATH], the edge term of the relaxed loss at [MATH] approximately equals, up to a constant, minus twice the cut expected from decoding [MATH] shots. This explains why schedules tuned with exact expectation values lose their advantage at realistic budgets, and yields a shot-aware schedule whose final sharpness is set by the shot budget. On five G-set graphs with [MATH] variables on [MATH] qubits, this schedule outperforms every published schedule at its target budget in all [MATH] paired comparisons of the decoded circuit output, owing to the sharpness at [MATH] shots and mostly to switching off the regularization at [MATH]; after a classical bit-swap search, it remains the best on average at [MATH] shots. Device noise damps the correlators by a factor [MATH], which amounts to a smaller shot budget [MATH]. On the IBM Heron processor ibm_fez, an all-to-all ansatz of the type used for the best published G-set results compiles to [MATH] CZ gates and decodes to a random cut, while our [MATH]-CZ hardware-native circuit, trained in simulation and sharpened to [MATH], retains up to [MATH] of the best-known cut. For new circuits, a damping and an offset calibrated on other circuits of the same graph predicted the decoded cuts at [MATH] shots to within [MATH].
tldr: This paper introduces a shot- and noise-aware schedule for Pauli correlation encoding to improve Max-Cut experiments on IBM's Heron quantum processor.
motivation: Pauli correlation encoding benchmarks typically assume exact expectation values, but real quantum computers estimate correlators from a finite number of shots, causing schedules tuned with exact values to lose their advantage at realistic budgets.
method: The authors show that the sharpness parameter acts as a hidden shot budget, derive a shot-aware schedule where final sharpness is set by the shot budget, and test it on five G-set graphs with 10 variables on IBM Heron using hardware-native circuits.
result: The shot-aware schedule outperforms all published schedules at target budgets in paired comparisons, and after a classical bit-swap search it remains best on average; noise is modeled as damping corresponding to a smaller effective shot budget, with a hardware-native circuit retaining a substantial fraction of the best-known cut.
conclusion: Accounting for shot noise and device noise is essential for tuning Pauli correlation encoding on near-term quantum processors, enabling better Max-Cut performance without exact expectation values.

title: Two-Photon Spatial Multiplexing: Image Encoding In Gaussian Noncircularity Of Light
authors: Wanting Hou, Zhiyuan Ye, Hong-Chao Liu, Jun Xiong, Kaige Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The search for new degrees of freedom (DoF) of light is central to advancing optical information encoding and multiplexing. Gaussian statistics are ubiquitous in nature, and here we unlock an unexpected statistical DoF in the joint noncircularity of Gaussian light. For a pair of Gaussian light fields, the covariance- and pseudocovariance-dominated two types of correlations dictate the propagation rules and the image-encoding responses, mapping optical information into coordinate-difference and coordinate-sum momentum spaces, respectively. A hybrid random-phase grating array enables the experimental preparation of noncircular Gaussian light with programmable coexistence, yielding X-shaped intensity correlations while subtly reducing the degree of second-order coherence. Two independently programmed images coexist in the same beams at identical wavelength and polarization, yet are selectively decoded through two-photon correlation geometry without physical filters. Remarkably, both images remain recoverable even when structured stray light is as intense as the signal. These results unlock a hidden statistical dimension of optical information encoding, transforming Gaussian fluctuations into a dual-channel information carrier and joint noncircularity into a programmable optical DoF.
tldr: This paper introduces a new statistical degree of freedom in the joint noncircularity of Gaussian light for two-photon spatial multiplexing, enabling dual-image encoding and decoding without physical filters.
motivation: The search for new degrees of freedom of light is central to advancing optical information encoding and multiplexing, and Gaussian statistics offer an unexplored statistical dimension for such tasks.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally exploit covariance- and pseudocovariance-dominated correlations in noncircular Gaussian light, prepared via a hybrid random-phase grating array, to map optical information into coordinate-difference and coordinate-sum momentum spaces.
result: Two independently programmed images coexist in the same beams at identical wavelength and polarization and are selectively decoded through two-photon correlation geometry, remaining recoverable even when structured stray light is as intense as the signal.
conclusion: This work unlocks a hidden statistical dimension of optical information encoding, transforming Gaussian fluctuations into a dual-channel information carrier and joint noncircularity into a programmable optical degree of freedom.

title: Selective Control And Imaging Of Higgs And Goldstone Modes With A Quantum Simulator
authors: Connie Miao, Pranjal Praneel, Thomas G. Kiely, Eliott Rosenberg, Nicole S. Ticea, Pedram Roushan, Erich Mueller, Andre G. Petukhov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We realize the mesoscopic Bose-Hubbard model at unit-filling on a two-dimensional array of transmon qubits and selectively excite collective modes associated with amplitude or phase fluctuations of the superfluid order parameter. We identify these modes respectively as the Higgs and Goldstone modes using complementary local observables, extracted from measuring the number of particles on each site. Modulation of the coupling between sites excites the Higgs mode, which we detect via the density of doubly occupied sites. In contrast, modulation of the local chemical potential with an appropriately chosen spatial profile excites the lowest-frequency Goldstone mode, which we detect via changes in the local density. The two modes have different symmetries and do not couple to one another. By varying the system geometry, we characterize the impact of finite system size on the evolution of both modes. In the thermodynamic limit, decay into a continuum of lower-energy excitations can obscure the Higgs response. In our mesoscopic system, however, the finite system size leads to spectral gaps and allows us to detect the Higgs mode as a coherent, long-lived excitation. Our work demonstrates how finite quantum simulators can isolate and probe physical phenomena that become difficult to resolve in the thermodynamic, large-scale limit.
tldr: Realized a mesoscopic Bose-Hubbard model on a 2D transmon qubit array to selectively excite and detect Higgs and Goldstone modes, showing finite-size effects stabilize the Higgs mode.
motivation: To probe collective excitations associated with amplitude and phase fluctuations of a superfluid order parameter, which become difficult to resolve in the thermodynamic limit due to decay into a continuum.
method: Using a two-dimensional array of transmon qubits at unit filling, modulate inter-site coupling to excite the Higgs mode and modulate local chemical potential with a spatial profile to excite the Goldstone mode, detecting them via local density and double occupancy measurements.
result: The Higgs mode is excited by coupling modulation and detected via double occupancy, while the Goldstone mode is excited by chemical potential modulation and detected via local density changes; the two modes decouple, and finite system size creates spectral gaps that allow coherent, long-lived detection of the Higgs mode.
conclusion: Demonstrates how finite quantum simulators can isolate and probe physical phenomena that are obscured in the thermodynamic, large-scale limit.

title: Strong Field Confinement In Air And Enhanced Optical Kerr Nonlinearity Of High-index Star-shaped Pore Membrane Metasurfaces
authors: Andrey V. Panov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The optical Kerr effect in high-refractive-index membrane metasurfaces patterned with a square lattice of five-pointed star-shaped pores is investigated numerically using gallium phosphide as a model material. The star geometry supports resonances with pronounced electromagnetic energy confinement, including an anapole state. The sharp tips of the star-shaped pores concentrate the electric energy density in air, exceeding that of Mie voids by a factor of seven. The effective second-order refractive index is enhanced by up to three orders of magnitude relative to bulk GaP, with the largest values obtained near the anapole resonances. The nonlinear response remains stable under polarization rotation and random misalignment of the nanoholes, indicating tolerance to fabrication imperfections. These results establish star-shaped pore lattices in freestanding membranes as a promising platform for nonlinear optics exploiting strong field confinement.
tldr: Numerical study of strong field confinement and enhanced optical Kerr nonlinearity in high-index star-shaped pore membrane metasurfaces, showing anapole resonances and robustness to fabrication imperfections.
motivation: To explore whether star-shaped pore geometries in freestanding high-index membranes can achieve strong electromagnetic confinement and large nonlinear enhancement for nonlinear optics applications.
method: Finite-element or similar numerical simulations of gallium phosphide metasurfaces with square lattices of five-pointed star-shaped pores, analyzing resonances, field confinement, and effective nonlinear refractive index.
result: Star-shaped pores concentrate electric energy in air up to seven times more than Mie voids, enhance the effective second-order refractive index by up to three orders of magnitude relative to bulk GaP, and remain stable under polarization rotation and misalignment.
conclusion: Star-shaped pore lattices in freestanding membranes are promising platforms for nonlinear optics exploiting strong field confinement, though the work remains classical photonics without direct quantum information relevance.

title: Coherent-State Integrals Beyond The Domain Of Operator Products
authors: Ghasem Asadi Cordshooli
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inserting a resolution of the identity between two operators turns a matrix element of their product into a phase-space integral. For unbounded operators the product need not exist on the vector at hand, while the integral may still converge. We follow this gap through the chain [MATH] of two-photon exponentials, where it can be traced completely. Five regions of parameter space appear: where the Bochner conditions of the strong formulation hold, where the product exists as a vector, where it exists as a sesquilinear form, where the coherent-state integral converges, and where the Fock-space series converges. The first three are strictly nested inside the intersection of the last two, and these two overlap without either containing the other. A single Hermite-type function agrees with the matrix element where it exists and with the integral and the series wherever they converge, so the integral carries the analytic continuation of the matrix element beyond the domain of the product and beyond the convergence of its Fock series. On the real slice of parameter space, an iterated form of the integral also reaches every point where the series converges. The analysis rests on a weak composition lemma whose hypotheses concern only the bra, the ket and the resolving family. For bounded chains the same identity is unconditional, and worked examples of that kind are given in a companion paper.
tldr: The paper mathematically analyzes coherent-state phase-space integrals of products of unbounded operators, showing they can converge even when the operator product does not exist as a vector or sesquilinear form, and characterizes the convergence regions.
motivation: Inserting a resolution of the identity between two operators turns a matrix element of their product into a phase-space integral, but for unbounded operators the product may fail to exist while the integral still converges.
method: The authors study a chain of two-photon exponentials, rigorously comparing five regions of parameter space defined by Bochner conditions, existence as a vector or sesquilinear form, convergence of the coherent-state integral, and convergence of the Fock-space series.
result: The first three regions are strictly nested inside the intersection of the last two, which overlap without containment; a single Hermite-type function agrees with the matrix element where it exists and with the integral and series where they converge, providing analytic continuation beyond the product domain.
conclusion: The coherent-state integral extends the analytic continuation of the matrix element beyond the domain of the operator product and beyond convergence of its Fock series, based on a weak composition lemma.

title: Generalized Fibonacci Gates Are Frobenius Algebras: A Proof Of Liu's Conjecture
authors: Aaron Sterling
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Liu introduced generalized Fibonacci gates on domains of size 3 and 4, proved that Holant problems built from them are tractable by a cut-and-merge algorithm, and conjectured that Fibonacci gates with matching polynomial-time algorithms exist on all higher domains. We extend the definition uniformly to every domain size [MATH] and show that a family of domain-[MATH] generalized Fibonacci gates is the same thing as a [MATH]-dimensional commutative Frobenius (equivalently, Artinian Gorenstein) algebra [MATH] equipped with an orthonormal basis containing [MATH]. Under this dictionary Liu's parameter constraints are exactly associativity of [MATH], a gate is an element [MATH], merging two gates is multiplication in [MATH], and the Holant value of a connected graph [MATH] is [MATH] for a fixed ``handle'' element [MATH]. This proves Liu's conjecture for every [MATH], with an algorithm whose cost is polynomial in [MATH] as well as in the graph. We also give a closure criterion for linear recurrences of any depth (a balance condition implies closure, and is necessary when the unit is a combination of the colours), and we map the landscape: semisimple algebras are exactly Liu's orthogonal frames, smoothable algebras with nilpotents are collided frames, and families whose algebra is not smoothable (``frameless'' families) exist exactly when [MATH]. Finally we show that every non-semisimple part of a family is invisible to the Holant on connected graphs with two or more independent cycles. This note states the results and sketches the proofs; the proofs of the main theorems are short and are given essentially in full.
tldr: The paper proves Liu's conjecture by establishing a bijection between generalized Fibonacci gates over any domain size and commutative Frobenius (Artinian Gorenstein) algebras, yielding polynomial-time algorithms for the associated Holant problems.
motivation: Liu introduced generalized Fibonacci gates on domains of size 3 and 4, proved the tractability of their Holant problems, and conjectured that analogous gates with matching polynomial-time algorithms exist on all higher domains; this work aims to resolve that conjecture.
method: The authors uniformly extend the definition of Fibonacci gates to every domain size and show that a family of such gates is equivalent to an M-dimensional commutative Frobenius algebra equipped with an orthonormal basis, under which gate merging becomes algebra multiplication and the Holant value reduces to an algebraic quantity; they also give a closure criterion for linear recurrences and classify families via smoothability of the algebra.
result: Liu's conjecture is proven for every domain size with an algorithm polynomial in both M and the graph, semisimple algebras are identified with Liu's orthogonal frames, nilpotent smoothable algebras with collided frames, frameless families exist exactly when M>4, and non-semisimple parts are shown to be invisible to the Holant on connected graphs with two or more independent cycles.
conclusion: The work provides a complete algebraic dictionary for generalized Fibonacci gates and settles Liu's conjecture, though the results belong to classical counting complexity and holographic algorithms rather than to any of the four quantum-focused research directions.

title: Anomalies, Higher Symmetries, And Homotopy Theory I: Crossed Precosheaves And A Nonabelian Cech Construction
authors: Shixiong Xu Anton Kapustin
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symmetries of a quantum field theory or a quantum lattice model are expected to be described not by a group but by a homotopy type, whose homotopy groups are the higher symmetry groups and whose Postnikov invariants encode 't Hooft anomalies. We propose a homotopy-theoretic definition of 't Hooft anomalies based on the structure of localized symmetries in the operator-algebraic approach. The input is a crossed precosheaf: a collection of groups attached to regions of space, equipped with pairings recording that the commutator of two transformations localized in two regions is localized in their intersection. To a crossed precosheaf and a finite family of regions we attach a pointed connected homotopy type, the Cech-Loday classifying space. As the family of regions ranges over finite covers of space, the classifying spaces form a pro-object in the homotopy category. There is a canonical map from the ordinary classifying space of the symmetry group to this pro-type. Composing this map with a group action gives an anomaly whose nontriviality obstructs gauging. In favorable cases, the Cech-Loday space is essentially independent of the cover. In such cases, the homotopy fiber of the canonical map is a candidate for the classifying space of the higher group of symmetries. We give examples of crossed precosheaves arising from gauge transformations in continuum field theory and from quantum cellular automata and finite-depth circuits. For quantum spin systems in one and two dimensions, our construction recovers the Else-Nayak index and its generalizations to two dimensions.
tldr: The paper proposes a homotopy-theoretic definition of 't Hooft anomalies using crossed precosheaves and a Cech-Loday classifying space, with examples from gauge theory and quantum cellular automata.
motivation: To describe higher symmetries and anomalies in quantum field theories and lattice models beyond ordinary group symmetry, using an operator-algebraic approach.
method: Defines crossed precosheaves as groups attached to regions with commutator pairings, constructs pointed connected homotopy types via a nonabelian Cech construction, and considers pro-objects over finite covers.
result: Recovers the Else-Nayak index for quantum spin systems in one and two dimensions and provides a framework where the anomaly obstructs gauging the symmetry.
conclusion: The Cech-Loday classifying space offers a general homotopy-theoretic tool for anomalies and higher symmetry classification, with potential applications to quantum lattice models.

title: A Reconstruction Of Michelson Interference From On--Off Detection Statistics
authors: Kim Myung-Whun
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper reconstructs the Michelson interference phenomenon based solely on the binary (on-off) statistics of a single-photon counter and macroscopic path-difference data, without the a priori assumptions of complex wave superposition or prior spectral information. In contrast to the conventional approach that assumes light as a continuous complex wave function and considers interference between them, this study focuses on the algebraic properties inherent in discrete detection statistics. We verify that the discrete response data collected across various path differences form a positive semi-definite matrix, and apply Herglotz's theorem to this result. Consequently, we show that the harmonic form of the interference fringe is not a consequence of adopting a wave model as an axiom, but rather it is uniquely decomposed into a cosine average of wavenumbers dictated by testable algebraic constraints satisfied by the statistical data. Through this approach, the logical basis of the interference phenomenon can be described by the characteristics of the binary data itself, perfectly aligning with the modern optical experimental environment that relies entirely on discrete event statistics.
tldr: The paper reconstructs Michelson interference from binary on-off single-photon detection statistics using a positive semidefinite matrix and Herglotz's theorem, avoiding wave-superposition assumptions.
motivation: To provide a logical basis for interference based solely on discrete event statistics, aligning with modern optical experiments that rely entirely on single-photon counting.
method: Collects on-off detection data across various path differences, verifies that the data form a positive semidefinite matrix, and applies Herglotz's theorem to decompose the fringe pattern into a cosine average of wavenumbers.
result: Shows that the harmonic form of the interference fringe is uniquely determined by algebraic constraints satisfied by the binary statistics, without assuming a complex wave model or prior spectral information.
conclusion: Interference phenomena can be described by the algebraic properties of discrete detection statistics, offering a statistical foundation that matches discrete-event experimental environments.

title: Bilinear Compressive Security With Finitely Many Samples
authors: Axel Flinth, Semira Einsele, Matilda Kylberg, Hubert Orlicki, Gerhard Wunder
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bilinear Compressive Security (BCS) is a lightweight encryption scheme that combines compressed sensing with a fresh random convolution filter to improve resistance against key-recovery attacks under key reuse. Previous work derived information-theoretic guarantees for BCS by relating key identifiability to phase retrieval under the assumption that an adversary has access to the full ciphertext distribution induced by the random filter. In practice, however, an adversary only observes finitely many encryptions, leaving the security of BCS in the finite-sample regime largely unexplored. In this paper, we study key recovery from only finitely many observations. We first develop a covariance-based attack that estimates the linear measurements from repeated encryptions of the same plaintext and subsequently recovers the secret measurement matrix. We analyze the estimation procedure and derive finite-sample guarantees together with corresponding sample-complexity bounds. We further investigate the complete attack experimentally and compare its observed recovery behavior with the previously established information-theoretic identifiability results. Our experiments show two qualitatively different recovery regimes on the structure of the measurement matrix. For dense matrices, including Gaussian matrices, the number of measurements required for successful recovery appears to grow linearly with the signal dimension. This differs from the worst-case behavior suggested by information theory. In contrast, for matrices with sparse rows, we observe a quadratic growth consistent with the theoretical bound. These results suggest that the sparsity structure of the measurement matrix plays an important role in the security of BCS and should be taken into account when selecting parameters and designing practical instances of the scheme.
tldr: This paper analyzes finite-sample key-recovery attacks on Bilinear Compressive Security, a classical compressed-sensing-based encryption scheme.
motivation: Previous information-theoretic security guarantees for BCS assumed access to the full ciphertext distribution, leaving open the practical finite-sample regime where an adversary sees only limited encryptions.
method: The authors develop a covariance-based attack that estimates linear measurements from repeated encryptions of the same plaintext and then recovers the secret measurement matrix, supported by finite-sample guarantees and sample-complexity bounds.
result: Experiments reveal two recovery regimes: dense matrices require sample complexity growing linearly with dimension, while sparse-row matrices show quadratic growth consistent with theoretical bounds.
conclusion: The sparsity structure of the measurement matrix critically affects BCS security and should inform parameter selection and practical design.

title: A Sociophysics Approach To Measuring Democracy In The Decision Making Of A Group: Three Indices
authors: Sudipto Roy
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A group does not usually consult all its members before every decision. This paper develops a quantitative framework for measuring how widely members are consulted in decision making within a group. Two kinds of records are considered: the number of members consulted for each decision and the number of decisions in which each member is consulted. From these records, two participation indices are defined, and their equality is proved analytically. A third index measures the fraction of decisions for which at least a specified percentage of members are consulted. The distribution of consultation levels is described using a discrete maximum-entropy model from statistical physics. Tail probabilities are used to obtain bounds for the main participation index. This study examines aggregate survey data from two groups. Their observed characteristics are broadly consistent with the patterns found across the full survey. Using binomial and Poisson calculations, the future probability that all members will be consulted for a decision is examined. Inequality in consultation among members is examined through Lorenz curves, the Gini coefficient and a normalised Shannon participation measure. The member-decision structure is represented as a bipartite network. Controlled simulations show that the same overall level of consultation can have different distributions among the members. The framework measures both the overall breadth of consultation and how consultation is distributed among the members. It therefore provides a quantitative sociophysical description of one measurable aspect of democracy in decision making within a group.
tldr: The paper proposes a sociophysical statistical framework with three indices to quantify how broadly group members are consulted in decision-making.
motivation: A group rarely consults all members before every decision, and there is a need for quantitative measures of democratic participation in group decisions.
method: The authors define two participation indices from consultation records, prove their equality, introduce a third index for threshold consultation, and model consultation distributions with a discrete maximum-entropy approach; they analyze survey data and run controlled simulations.
result: The indices show equality analytically, bounds via tail probabilities, and inequality measured by Lorenz curves, Gini coefficient, and normalized Shannon entropy; simulations reveal that the same overall consultation level can yield different intra-group distributions.
conclusion: The framework provides a quantitative sociophysical description of one aspect of democracy in group decision-making, though it lies outside quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: On Optimal Wannier Decay In Dimension Three
authors: Simon Becker, Zhongkai Tao, Mengxuan Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a Chern nontrivial Bloch bundle over the three torus, we construct an orthonormal Wannier basis with the optimal pointwise decay [MATH]. All but one of the generators decay exponentially. This resolves the question left open in arXiv:2505.01999.
tldr: The paper constructs an orthonormal Wannier basis for a Chern nontrivial Bloch bundle over the three-torus with optimal pointwise decay, where all but one generator decay exponentially.
motivation: Wannier functions are central to understanding localization in topological insulators, and the optimal decay rate for Chern nontrivial bundles in three dimensions was an open problem.
method: The authors explicitly construct an orthonormal Wannier basis and rigorously analyze its pointwise decay properties, proving exponential decay for all but one generator.
result: They achieve the optimal pointwise decay for the Wannier basis on a three-dimensional Chern nontrivial Bloch bundle, with exactly one generator failing to decay exponentially.
conclusion: This work resolves the open question posed in arXiv:2505.01999 and advances the mathematical theory of Wannier localization for topologically nontrivial bundles.

title: Weak Private Information Retrieval For Graph-based Storage Under $\epsilon$-privacy
authors: Prasad Krishnan Jayesh Seshadri
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The problem of Private Information Retrieval (PIR) across graph-based replicated systems has seen a surge of interest in recent literature. In such systems, servers are modeled as the vertices of a graph, and each file is represented by an edge connecting the pair of servers that store it. While previous research on Graph-PIR (G-PIR) has focused mostly on perfect information-theoretic privacy, relaxing this constraint has the potential for significantly higher retrieval rates. In this work, we consider the setting of Graph-based Weak Private Information Retrieval (G-WPIR), under an [MATH]-privacy metric. We adapt an existing G-WPIR scheme for arbitrary graphs to analyze its performance under the [MATH]-privacy metric. Additionally, we establish a lower bound on the expected download cost for arbitrary graphs under the [MATH]-privacy metric and derive from it an explicit rate upper bound for complete graphs. Finally, we show the achievable rate-privacy trade-offs for two specific graph classes---complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs.
tldr: The paper analyzes weak private information retrieval in graph-based replicated storage under an ε-privacy metric, deriving achievable rates and lower bounds for arbitrary graphs and explicit trade-offs for complete and complete bipartite graphs.
motivation: Previous work on graph-based PIR has focused on perfect information-theoretic privacy, and relaxing this constraint to ε-privacy may enable significantly higher retrieval rates.
method: The authors adapt an existing G-WPIR scheme for arbitrary graphs to the ε-privacy setting, establish a lower bound on expected download cost for arbitrary graphs, and derive an explicit rate upper bound for complete graphs.
result: They obtain achievable rate-privacy trade-offs for complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs, along with a general lower bound on expected download cost under ε-privacy.
conclusion: The work demonstrates how weak privacy metrics can improve retrieval rates in graph-based PIR systems, providing new bounds and trade-off characterizations for specific graph classes.

title: On Generators And Relations For $O_n^\circ(V)$ In Higher-level Zhu Algebras, Part I
authors: Nathan Vander Werf
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the circle-relation subspace [MATH] in the defining relations of the level-[MATH] Zhu algebra of a vertex operator algebra [MATH]. We assemble the residue relations generating [MATH] into generating functions and obtain an explicit recursion that replaces every sufficiently deep mode by retained modes with indices at least [MATH], modulo [MATH]. This recursion is encoded in a left truncated field [MATH]. Since such mode replacements are valid only in the leftmost position of an operator product, we prove the replacement, derivative, commutator, and one-step iterate identities for [MATH] needed for finite-length calculations. For a finite homogeneous strong generating set [MATH], we define the finite-length circle subspaces [MATH] and their plus subspaces. We formulate a finite-length conjecture under an explicit auxiliary-degree hypothesis and a separate termwise conjecture for the correction residues of one-sided iterates. We prove reductions to the [MATH] strip and to last vacuum mode [MATH], recover the length-one relation spaces, and give explicit Virasoro computations at word length two for [MATH] and [MATH]. The [MATH] identities are the input for the companion paper (Part II).
tldr: A pure-mathematics study of the circle-relation subspace in the defining relations of higher-level Zhu algebras of vertex operator algebras, providing generating functions, recursions, and finite-length conjectures.
motivation: The paper aims to make the defining relations of level-n Zhu algebras computationally tractable by reducing deep modes to retained modes, providing the algebraic machinery needed for finite-length calculations.
method: Residue relations are assembled into generating functions encoded in a left truncated field, and replacement, derivative, commutator, and one-step iterate identities are proven to support finite-length computations; reductions to the strip and last vacuum mode are derived.
result: Explicit recursions replacing sufficiently deep modes modulo the circle-relation subspace are obtained, length-one relation spaces are recovered, and explicit Virasoro computations at word length two are given for specific cases.
conclusion: These identities form the algebraic input for the companion paper (Part II), extending the structural understanding of Zhu algebra relations in vertex operator algebra theory.

title: Thompson Sampling For Learning In Zero-Sum Games
authors: Kenshi Abe, Kaito Ariu, Po-An Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thompson sampling (TS) achieves logarithmic and asymptotically optimal regret in classical stochastic bandits, but its behavior in multi-agent learning remains less understood. We study TS in an unknown finite two-player zero-sum matrix game with Gaussian bandit feedback. Under centralized self-play, TS samples a single payoff matrix from the posterior and plays a Nash equilibrium of the sampled game. For every fixed zero-sum game with a unique Nash equilibrium, we show that the expected cumulative duality gap is [MATH]. The rate improves to [MATH] for pure equilibria. We then identify the exact coefficient of the [MATH] term, which depends only on the equilibrium strategies and the noise level. We also establish a minimax lower bound matching the square-root dependence on [MATH] and an instance-dependent lower bound matching the logarithmic dependence on [MATH] for a class of games with a unique pure equilibrium. Experiments support the predicted rates and coefficient.
tldr: The paper analyzes Thompson sampling in two-player zero-sum matrix games with Gaussian bandit feedback, deriving regret bounds and lower bounds.
motivation: Thompson sampling is well understood in single-agent stochastic bandits, but its theoretical behavior in multi-agent learning settings such as zero-sum games remains less clear.
method: Under centralized self-play, Thompson sampling samples a single payoff matrix from the posterior and plays a Nash equilibrium of the sampled game; the authors analyze expected cumulative duality gap and establish minimax and instance-dependent lower bounds.
result: They obtain logarithmic and asymptotically optimal regret rates, identify the exact coefficient of the leading term, and show improved rates for pure equilibria, matching lower bounds for square-root dependence and logarithmic dependence.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous theoretical characterization of Thompson sampling in zero-sum games, supported by experiments confirming the predicted rates and coefficient.

title: Polynomial Separation Of A Shared Tensor Leg And Matrix Multiplication In Arbitrary Characteristic
authors: Houxi L\"u
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We improve the shared-leg separation construction in Proposition 3.1 of OpenAI, *An Upper Bound of [MATH] for the Matrix Multiplication Exponent* (October 2, 2026). If [MATH] tensor blocks have a common first space and independent matched sectors on their other two spaces, then [MATH] copies of their matched sum degenerate to the full direct sum of the blocks, each tensored with an [MATH]-dimensional dot product. For [MATH], this reduces the number of source copies from [MATH] to [MATH]. The construction uses polynomial interpolation and truncated local substitution, with no roots of unity or factorial denominators. It works over every field containing enough distinct elements. We verify that the remaining spectral and discrete-growth arguments of the cited preprint are independent of characteristic. Over an algebraic closure, the replacement therefore gives [MATH] in every characteristic.
tldr: The paper improves a tensor-leg separation construction used to bound the matrix multiplication exponent, extending it to arbitrary characteristic via polynomial interpolation and truncated local substitution.
motivation: The work aims to strengthen a recent upper bound on the matrix multiplication exponent by making the shared-leg separation construction independent of roots of unity and valid over fields of arbitrary characteristic.
method: It uses polynomial interpolation and truncated local substitution to reduce the number of source copies in a shared-leg tensor construction, avoiding roots of unity and factorial denominators.
result: For a specific case the number of source copies is reduced, and the spectral and discrete-growth arguments are verified to be characteristic-independent, yielding an improved exponent bound over any algebraic closure.
conclusion: The construction generalizes previous tensor separation techniques to arbitrary characteristic, potentially advancing algebraic complexity bounds for matrix multiplication.

title: What You Earn From What You Learn: Characterization And Complexity Of The Value Of Information
authors: Ratip Emin Berker, Ioannis Anagnostides, Emanuel Tewolde, Brian Hu Zhang, Tuomas Sandholm, Vincent Conitzer
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the value of information in extensive-form decision problems: the largest multiplicative gain that a decision maker can obtain from an information refinement, taken over all payoff environments. This measures the structural importance of information disentangled from any particular payoff specification, and generalizes the notion of value of recall recently introduced by Berker et al. (AAAI'25). We establish a unifying characterization of the value of information under any information refinement, uncovering an intriguing connection to the maximum fractional chromatic number over a certain family of conflict graphs. We then employ our characterization to elucidate the complexity of two central information refinements. First, for the value of perfect information in perfect-recall decision problems, we find that the relevant conflict graphs are cographs, so the fractional chromatic number collapses to the clique number. Even though the clique number is tractable for a given cograph, we show that the additional layer of optimization (over the family of graphs) makes computing the value of perfect information NP-complete. On the positive side, we prove fixed-parameter tractability in terms of the degree of imperfect information. Second, for the value of recall in imperfect-recall decision problems (with no absentmindedness), we first show that the value of recall can realize the fractional chromatic number of any graph. Interestingly, this implies that, unlike the value of perfect information, the value of recall can take fractional values. Building on this reduction, we then establish S2P-completeness. This addresses questions left open by Berker et al. (AAAI'25)---both on the characterization and the complexity of the value of recall---and shows that computing the value of recall is strictly harder than the value of perfect information.
tldr: The paper characterizes and analyzes the complexity of the value of information in extensive-form decision problems, connecting it to fractional chromatic number and proving NP-completeness and S2P-completeness results.
motivation: To quantify the structural importance of information in decision problems independent of specific payoffs, generalizing the value of recall.
method: They establish a unifying characterization of the value of information via conflict graphs and fractional chromatic number, then analyze complexity for perfect and imperfect recall.
result: Value of perfect information is NP-complete but fixed-parameter tractable; value of recall is S2P-complete and can be fractional.
conclusion: Computing value of recall is strictly harder than value of perfect information, resolving open questions.

title: Joint Identification, Transmission, And Sensing Over State-Dependent Channels With Noiseless Feedback
authors: Vida Gholamian, Marcel A. Mross, Roberto Ferrara, Eduard A. Jorswieck, Christian Deppe
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a discrete memoryless state-dependent channel with noiseless feedback, where the transmitter uses randomized encoding to jointly perform message transmission, identification, and state sensing. In this setting, the transmitter sends a conventional transmission message and an identification message while estimating the unknown channel state sequence under an average distortion constraint. We establish a single-letter characterization of the randomized identification-transmission-sensing capacity-distortion region. The result reveals a single-letter separation structure: the communication rates are determined by the averaged channel, subject to the sensing-induced constraint on admissible input distributions. Specifically, the transmission rate is characterized by mutual information, while the identification rate is characterized by output entropy under the same distortion constraint. The achievability proof combines constant-composition transmission coding, output partitioning, and combinatorial identification coding, while the converse follows from an averaged-channel reduction, distortion lower bounds, and feedback-identification converse arguments.
tldr: The paper derives a single-letter capacity-distortion region for joint message transmission, identification, and state sensing over a state-dependent discrete memoryless channel with noiseless feedback.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits of simultaneously communicating a message, identifying a message, and estimating an unknown channel state under an average distortion constraint when noiseless feedback is available.
method: Achievability uses randomized encoding, constant-composition transmission coding, output partitioning, and combinatorial identification coding; the converse relies on an averaged-channel reduction, distortion lower bounds, and feedback-identification converse arguments.
result: A single-letter characterization is established, revealing a separation structure where the transmission rate is given by mutual information, the identification rate by output entropy, and both are constrained by the sensing-induced distortion constraint on admissible input distributions.
conclusion: The separation result shows that communication rates are determined by the averaged channel subject to sensing constraints, advancing classical Shannon theory for joint transmission, identification, and sensing with feedback.

title: A Nontrivial Lattice Scalar Quantum Field Model
authors: P. A. Faria Da Veiga, R. Mistry, M. O'carroll
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new Euclidean quantum model with zero-spin scaled scalar fields on a spacetime hypercubic lattice, which we refer to as the hybrid model. The model coupling parameters are the hopping parameter [MATH] and the field interaction coupling [MATH]. Using the technique of lattice scaled fields, with a noncanonical scaling that corresponds to a partial renormalization (wave function renormalization), we show that the partition function of this model satisfies both thermodynamic and ultraviolet stability bounds, with constants which are uniform in the lattice volume [MATH] and the lattice spacing [MATH]. As a consequence, the model has a finite free energy per degree of freedom in the thermodynamic limit [MATH], at least in the subsequential sense. Subsequently, we can also take the ultraviolet or continuum limit [MATH]. Besides the finiteness property of the free energy, for sufficiently small values of the model coupling parameters [MATH] and [MATH], we show the model satisfies Osterwalder-Schrader positivity and construct the underlying physical quantum mechanical Hilbert space, and, using a polymer expansion, we show correlations also remain bounded in the thermodynamic limit. Finally, we perturbatively compute an infinite volume truncated four-point correlation showing it is nonzero. Noting that, for fixed [MATH], perturbation series in [MATH] and [MATH] converges, these results are sufficient to show that our hybrid model makes sense as a lattice quantum field theory in spacetime dimension [MATH], with possible extensions to other higher values of [MATH].
tldr: The paper constructs and analyzes a Euclidean lattice scalar quantum field model with scaled fields, proving stability bounds, a finite free energy, Osterwalder-Schrader positivity, and nonvanishing truncated four-point correlations.
motivation: The authors introduce a new lattice scalar field model to study whether a nontrivial Euclidean quantum field theory can be rigorously constructed in spacetime dimension d = 4.
method: They use lattice scaled fields with a noncanonical scaling corresponding to partial wave-function renormalization, thermodynamic and ultraviolet stability bounds, polymer expansions, and perturbative computations.
result: The partition function satisfies uniform stability bounds, the model has a finite free energy per degree of freedom in both thermodynamic and continuum limits, satisfies Osterwalder-Schrader positivity, and yields a nonzero truncated four-point correlation.
conclusion: The hybrid model is shown to make sense as a lattice quantum field theory in four dimensions, with possible extensions to higher dimensions, though it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: GeONet: Geometry-Encoded Operator Network For Predicting Flow In Heterogeneous Porous Media
authors: Md Lal Mamud, Maruti K. Mudunuru, Yucheng Fu, Aramy Troung, Satish Karra, Ivani Patel, Arunima Bhattacharjee, Tamas Varga, Pratanu Roy, Michael Penwarden, Rajesh K. Singh, Arjun Chakrawal, Kalyana B. Nakshatrala, Christof Meile, Erin Rooney, Glenn Hammond
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rapid prediction of pressure-driven flow in microfluidic porous media is important for experimental design, tracer-test interpretation, and digital-twin development for subsurface energy and critical mineral applications. High-fidelity simulations resolve geometry-controlled flow but are computationally expensive across large geometry ensembles. Here, we introduce GeONet, a Geometry-Encoded Operator Network that predicts steady-state pressure fields by jointly representing material properties, spatial coordinates, and solid--void geometry. GeONet extends the Branch--Trunk architecture with a dedicated Leaf Network encoding the binary domain mask through multiscale features. The Branch Network represents porosity and permeability, the Trunk Network combines coordinates with local geometric descriptors and random Fourier features, and a gated DeepMixer integrates these representations to predict pressure. GeONet was trained and evaluated using 5,000 PFLOTRAN simulations of heterogeneous Reduced Complexity Platform domains, comprising nearly 30 TB of data. Comparisons with pore-scale Stokes solutions across three geometries yielded Pearson correlations of 0.987--0.991 and [MATH] values of 0.974--0.982, supporting PFLOTRAN as reference data. Under matched partitions and two-stage hyperparameter optimization, GeONet substantially outperformed a boundary-condition-aware DeepONet baseline. Across three held-out domains, GeONet achieved NRMSE of 0.0381--0.0500, MAPE of 1.76--2.59%, and [MATH] of 0.9673--0.9822, versus 0.1483--0.2040, 7.81--10.45%, and 0.5658--0.7126 for DeepONet, respectively. On three additional unseen geometries, GeONet achieved NRMSE of 0.0448--0.0676 and [MATH] of 0.9511--0.9770. These results demonstrate improved accuracy, pressure-range preservation, and cross-geometry generalization through explicit geometry encoding.
tldr: GeONet is a geometry-encoded operator network that predicts steady-state pressure fields in heterogeneous porous media using DeepONet-style branch-trunk architecture with a leaf network for binary domain masks.
motivation: High-fidelity simulations of pressure-driven flow in microfluidic porous media are computationally expensive, creating a need for fast surrogate models that generalize across geometries for experimental design and digital twins.
method: The authors extend the Branch-Trunk operator network with a Leaf Network encoding binary domain geometry via multiscale features, using PFLOTRAN simulations (5,000 domains, ~30 TB) for training and comparing against Stokes solutions and a DeepONet baseline.
result: GeONet achieved NRMSE of 0.0381–0.0676 and R² of 0.9511–0.9822 on held-out and unseen geometries, substantially outperforming a boundary-condition-aware DeepONet baseline.
conclusion: Explicit geometry encoding improves accuracy, pressure-range preservation, and cross-geometry generalization for predicting flow in heterogeneous porous media.

title: An Improved Lower Bound For The Minimum-autocorrelation Constant
authors: Enhao Gu Shenai Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct nonnegative bounded compactly supported functions on the real line that give the lower bound [MATH] for the minimum-autocorrelation constant. This improves the explicitly certified bound [MATH] reported by Russell. The construction combines a point mass with a monotone degree-ten polynomial density; a one-sided atom-removal argument then produces ordinary functions. Its numerical content reduces to exact rational polynomial identities and 20 Bernstein subinterval certificates. The finite certificate, actual overlap integrals, admissibility, mass formula, and ordinary-function witness bounds have been formalized in Lean 4.19.0; the pinned proof sources and recorded audit are supplied. The passage to the supremum constant is given separately as a mathematical argument. As applications, the same construction yields an upper bound below [MATH] for the large-multiplicity generalized-difference-basis coefficient and a feasible squared mass below [MATH] for a continuous sparse-ruler relaxation. An appendix quantifies the loss under independent sampling followed by completion. No improved bound for the complete sparse ruler constant, or global optimality of the construction, is asserted.
tldr: The paper constructs nonnegative compactly supported functions to improve the certified lower bound for the minimum-autocorrelation constant.
motivation: It aims to improve upon Russell's explicitly certified bound using an explicit and formally verified construction.
method: The construction combines a point mass with a monotone degree-ten polynomial density, then uses a one-sided atom-removal argument and Bernstein subinterval certificates, with formalization in Lean 4.19.0.
result: The new lower bound improves the previous certified value, and applications yield an upper bound for the large-multiplicity generalized-difference-basis coefficient and a feasible squared mass for a sparse-ruler relaxation.
conclusion: The work provides a certified improvement for autocorrelation and sparse-ruler constants, but it does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimization For One, Feasibility For Most: Decoupling Optimization From Feasibility In Chance-Constrained Programs
authors: Justin Dumouchelle, Shunyu Yao, Beste Basciftci, Thiago Serra
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chance-constrained stochastic programs (CCSPs) require solutions that satisfy uncertain constraints with high probability. Standard approaches either embed scenarios directly into optimization by considering sample average approximation (SAA)-based reformulations, growing prohibitively expensive and often failing to find feasible solutions; or employ conservative reformulations that guarantee feasibility but sacrifice objective quality by design. We propose ACCESS (Adaptive Chance-Constrained Exploration via Structured Sampling), a structured sampling framework that decouples optimization from feasibility evaluation. First, high-quality candidate solutions are generated by solving many inexpensive single-scenario subproblems, avoiding sampling directly in the constrained high-dimensional solution space. Second, feasibility is assessed separately via large-scale batched simulation over a massive number of scenarios, which is naturally amenable to GPU parallelism. That reduces the search from a high-dimensional solution space to a two-dimensional parameter space controlling conservatism and scenario diversity; while concentrating on candidates near the feasibility boundary, where high-quality feasible solutions lie. We also introduce a variant, ACCESS([MATH]), which provides certified feasibility guarantees with probability [MATH]. Experiments across three benchmark classes and five scenario distributions show that ACCESS matches or exceeds the best objective found by any method in nearly every setting, while ACCESS([MATH]) is empirically feasible on every instance. The conservative reformulations remain several percent worse in objective, and SAA is frequently infeasible while taking an order of magnitude longer on the harder benchmarks.
tldr: The paper proposes ACCESS, a sampling-based framework for chance-constrained stochastic programs that decouples candidate generation from feasibility evaluation to improve scalability and solution quality.
motivation: Chance-constrained stochastic programs are often solved via sample average approximation, which becomes prohibitively expensive and may fail to find feasible solutions, or via conservative reformulations that sacrifice objective quality.
method: ACCESS first generates high-quality candidate solutions by solving many inexpensive single-scenario subproblems, then evaluates feasibility separately through large-scale batched GPU-parallel simulation, reducing the search to a two-dimensional parameter space controlling conservatism and scenario diversity.
result: Across three benchmark classes and five scenario distributions, ACCESS matches or exceeds the best objective found by any method in nearly every setting, while the ACCESS variant with certified feasibility guarantees is empirically feasible on every instance; conservative reformulations are several percent worse in objective, and SAA is often infeasible and an order of magnitude slower on harder benchmarks.
conclusion: Decoupling optimization from feasibility evaluation enables efficient and effective solutions for chance-constrained stochastic programs, outperforming standard SAA and conservative reformulation baselines.

title: $L^p_\mu$-Normed Spaces Of Bounded Multilinear Operator
authors: Filippo de Feo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the spaces of bounded multilinear operators [MATH] endowed with [MATH]-norms, where [MATH] are normed spaces and [MATH] is a measure with [MATH]-moments. These are norms without taking a quotient, under suitable support conditions. The topology induced coincides with the strong operator and compact-open topologies on operator-norm-bounded subsets. Furthermore, we identify the completion of these spaces with spaces of Hilbert--Schmidt operators on the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) for [MATH]; with iterated [MATH]-radonifying multilinear operators on the RKHS in the Gaussian case, for general [MATH].
tldr: The paper studies L^p_mu-normed spaces of bounded multilinear operators, characterizing their topology and completions via Hilbert-Schmidt and radonifying operators on reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces.
motivation: The author aims to develop a general framework for bounded multilinear operators equipped with L^p_mu norms, extending known topological and completion results under suitable support and moment conditions.
method: The analysis uses normed space theory, measure-theoretic L^p_mu constructions, strong operator and compact-open topologies, and identifying completions with spaces of Hilbert-Schmidt or iterated p-radonifying multilinear operators on RKHS.
result: The induced topology coincides with the strong operator and compact-open topologies on operator-norm-bounded subsets, and the completion is identified with Hilbert-Schmidt operators on the RKHS in general, or iterated p-radonifying multilinear operators in the Gaussian case.
conclusion: The work provides a functional-analytic characterization of L^p_mu-normed multilinear operator spaces, with no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Pointwise Minimax Lower Bounds Under A Multi-index Constraint: The Price Of An Unknown Orientation
authors: Nora Serdyukova
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider nonparametric regression with random design and non-Gaussian noise, where the regression function has the multi-index form [MATH] with an unknown link [MATH] in an anisotropic H\"older class and an unknown matrix [MATH] with [MATH] orthonormal rows. For estimation of [MATH] at a fixed point we prove that the minimax risk is bounded from below by a multiple of [MATH], where [MATH] is the harmonic mean of the smoothness indices of the link divided by [MATH]. For [MATH] this extends a Gaussian white noise result to regression. The main new case is [MATH], where no dimension reduction takes place: the logarithmic factor still appears as soon as the link is anisotropic and the orientation of its axes is unknown. In contrast, when the link is isotropic with smoothness index at most one, the class is rotation invariant up to a constant and the classical rate without logarithm is attained. The logarithmic loss is therefore caused by the unknown orientation of the directions in which the function is least smooth.
tldr: The paper proves minimax lower bounds for nonparametric multi-index regression when the link function is anisotropic and the orientation of its axes is unknown, showing a logarithmic price in the estimation rate.
motivation: Multi-index models are important for dimension reduction in nonparametric regression, but the effect of an unknown orientation of the index space on minimax rates is not fully understood.
method: The authors consider random design and non-Gaussian noise, assume an anisotropic Hölder class for the link and an unknown orthonormal matrix, and derive pointwise minimax lower bounds.
result: For estimation at a fixed point, the minimax risk has a lower bound with a logarithmic factor when the link is anisotropic and its orientation is unknown, even when no dimension reduction occurs; this extends a Gaussian white noise result to regression.
conclusion: The logarithmic loss is caused by the unknown orientation of the least-smooth directions, while rotation-invariant isotropic cases attain the classical rate without the logarithm.

title: Weight-adapted Anova Kernels For High-dimensional Periodic Approximation
authors: Zhengjie Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we construct normalized periodic kernels from univariate functions satisfying suitable moment conditions and derive sufficient conditions for high-order convolution approximation. Two computable quasi-interpolation schemes are obtained by discretizing the convolution integral using either a full tensor grid or random samples. In each case, the analysis separates the continuous convolution error from the error introduced by discretization. The contribution of kernel energy to the error exposes the dimensional dependence of tensor-product kernels and motivates our weight-adapted ANOVA constructions. Under suitable summability conditions on the weights, we establish convolution error and kernel energy estimates that yield dimension-uniform error bounds for the resulting quasi-interpolants. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical convergence rates and illustrate the effect of coordinate weighting on dimensional dependence.
tldr: The paper constructs weight-adapted ANOVA periodic kernels and quasi-interpolation schemes for high-dimensional function approximation with dimension-uniform error bounds.
motivation: High-dimensional periodic approximation suffers from the curse of dimensionality, and tensor-product kernels introduce strong dimensional dependence that needs to be mitigated.
method: Normalized periodic kernels are built from univariate functions with moment conditions, and convolution approximation is discretized via full tensor grids or random samples; ANOVA weight adaptation is used to control dimensional dependence.
result: Under suitable weight summability conditions, convolution error and kernel energy estimates yield dimension-uniform error bounds for the quasi-interpolants, corroborated by numerical experiments.
conclusion: Weight-adapted ANOVA constructions enable effective high-dimensional periodic approximation with provable dimension-independent convergence rates.

title: Physical Layer Anomaly Detection Via Adaptive Gaussian Mixture Model
authors: Mamady Delamou, Luan Chen, Arsenia Chorti
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physical-layer spoofing attacks pose a critical threat to wireless localization systems by manipulating channel state information (CSI). Detecting such attacks becomes particularly challenging when the attacker and the legitimate node are spatially proximate, as their CSI characteristics become increasingly similar. To address this challenge in indoor scenarios, we propose an adaptive Gaussian mixture model (GMM)-based detection framework that learns legitimate CSI patterns and detects spatial inconsistency through statistical anomaly detection. Using a massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) experimental dataset with 64 uniform linear array (ULA) antenna and 5 mm spatial resolution, we evaluated our detector against CSI spoofing attacks with spatial displacements ranging from 50 mm to 450 mm. The adaptive GMM achieves 95-98% detection rate for displacements above 150 mm while maintaining 1% false alarm rate. We benchmark our approach against conventional GMM, local outlier factor (LOF), one-class support vector machine (SVM) and k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) classifiers, demonstrating overall superior detection performance of our proposed classifier.
tldr: The paper proposes an adaptive Gaussian mixture model framework for detecting physical-layer spoofing attacks in wireless localization by learning legitimate channel state information patterns.
motivation: Physical-layer spoofing attacks threaten wireless localization systems by manipulating channel state information, and detection becomes especially difficult when the attacker is spatially close to the legitimate node.
method: It uses an adaptive Gaussian mixture model to learn legitimate CSI patterns and detect spatial inconsistency via statistical anomaly detection, evaluated on a massive MIMO dataset with a 64-antenna uniform linear array.
result: The adaptive GMM achieves 95–98% detection rate for displacements above 150 mm while maintaining a 1% false alarm rate, outperforming conventional GMM, local outlier factor, one-class SVM, and k-nearest neighbors.
conclusion: The adaptive GMM framework provides an effective and superior approach for physical-layer spoofing detection in indoor wireless localization scenarios.

title: The Gap Between Average-Case And Worst-Case Complexity
authors: Halley Goldberg, Jinqiao Hu, Zhenjian Lu, Jingyi Lyu, Igor C. Oliveira
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the average-case complexity of [MATH] is a central goal in complexity theory and cryptography. A necessary milestone is to understand the corresponding average-case versus worst-case question for the polynomial hierarchy ([MATH]). In a celebrated result, Hirahara [Hir21] proved that if every distributional problem in [MATH] is easy on average, then every language in [MATH] admits worst-case algorithms running in time [MATH]. Remarkably, although the statement of Hirahara's theorem makes no reference to meta-complexity, all known proofs appear to use time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity and its associated meta-computational problems in an essential way. We show that the reliance on techniques and perspectives from meta-complexity is not simply a coincidence. Building on previous work of Hirahara [Hir20] and on a recent result of Hu, Lu, and Oliveira [HLO25], we prove that relating the average-case and worst-case complexities of [MATH] is in fact equivalent to a purely meta-computational implication: efficient algorithms for a standard gap version of [MATH] with [MATH] oracle access imply efficient algorithms for a mild gap version. Crucially, in these promise problems the standard gap separates a YES instance with time bound [MATH] from a NO instance with time bound [MATH], whereas the mild gap keeps the YES threshold [MATH] and moves the NO threshold to [MATH]. Together with prior work, this equivalence points to the study of gap reductions as a potentially promising route toward understanding the relation between average-case and worst-case complexity. We make progress by proving that the gap in running time can be eliminated in the average-case setting. Finally, we prove that in the worst-case setting any efficient reduction between the two problems must use nonrelativizing techniques.
tldr: The paper proves an equivalence between relating average-case and worst-case complexity for the polynomial hierarchy and a purely meta-computational implication about gap problems involving time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity.
