motivation: Understanding average-case complexity and cryptography motivates the long-standing question of whether worst-case and average-case complexity for the polynomial hierarchy can be related, a problem whose known proofs rely essentially on meta-complexity.
method: Building on Hirahara's work and Hu-Lu-Oliveira, the authors establish equivalences between average-case vs. worst-case complexity of PH and algorithms for a standard gap version of MCSP with oracle access implying algorithms for a mild gap version, and analyze the gap in running time.
result: They show that the gap in running time can be eliminated in the average-case setting, while in the worst-case setting any efficient reduction between the two problems must use nonrelativizing techniques.
conclusion: The work indicates that gap reductions are a promising route for understanding average-case versus worst-case complexity, and that meta-complexity is not merely a coincidence in this context.

title: Hopfield Networks In Non-volatile Memory
authors: Ulya R. Karpuzcu Patrick Miller
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many important computational workloads are bound by the performance of the memory system that supplies data to conventional processors. Compute in Memory (CiM) promises to circumvent this bottleneck by performing the processing within the memory. Neural Networks are memory-bound, and a notable example of such is the Hopfield Network. This work explores the design space of non-volatile computing-in-memory (NV-CiM) architectures using an instruction-level simulator to evaluate application mappings and workload-driven architectural adaptations. The exploration examines the resulting design trade-offs and includes theoretical comparisons with representative CPU and GPU architectures.
tldr: This paper explores the design space of non-volatile compute-in-memory (NV-CiM) architectures for Hopfield networks using an instruction-level simulator, comparing them against CPU and GPU baselines.
motivation: Many computational workloads, particularly neural networks like Hopfield networks, are memory-bandwidth bound, and compute-in-memory promises to overcome this bottleneck by performing processing directly within memory.
method: The authors use an instruction-level simulator to evaluate application mappings and workload-driven architectural adaptations across a range of NV-CiM design points, and perform theoretical comparisons with representative CPU and GPU architectures.
result: The study characterizes the resulting design trade-offs in NV-CiM architectures for Hopfield network workloads and quantifies their theoretical advantages over conventional CPU and GPU designs.
conclusion: NV-CiM architectures offer a promising avenue for accelerating memory-bound Hopfield network workloads, with the design space exploration illuminating key trade-offs for future architecture development.

title: Mission (Im)Possible: Towards Autonomous Discovery Of Autopilot Logic Flaws In Open-Source Drone Frameworks
authors: Ziyi Liang, Zichuan Li, Bin Yuan, Deqing Zou, Luyi Xing
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous drones are increasingly deployed in safety-critical tasks, yet their autopilot software can still contain subtle logic flaws that lead to unsafe behaviors. These flaws are difficult to discover with existing techniques because they often depend on semantic relationships across modules, commands, and runtime state, and rarely manifest as crashes or detectable failures. With recent advances in LLMs, we observe that, when equipped with essential domain knowledge and carefully crafted context, LLMs demonstrate strong capabilities in understanding the high-level semantics of autopilot systems, making them suitable for logic flaw discovery. However, LLMs are limited by their context and can be biased to the vulnerabilities frequently occurs in training dataset, while logic flaws often require higher-level semantic bug oracles to identify their existence. To bridge the gap, we present Impossible Mission Finder (IMF), a multi-agent system combining static analysis, dynamic execution and log analysis, that supports fully automated identify, test, and validate logic flaws in autonomous vehicles. IMF primarily contains three LLM agents, it first uses the auditor agent to propose logic flaw hypothesis based on carefully-crafted program slicing, then it launches tester agents to write and execute test cases for each candidate, and finally it spawns the log analyzer agent to validate the execution log against the flaw hypothesis. This enables IMF dynamically validate bug oracles in a case-by-case manner, making it suitable for discovering logic flaws that do not have a unified pattern. We evaluated IMF on two widely used open-source autopilot systems, PX4 and Ardupilot, leading to 105 previously unknown logic flaws, that can cause unsafe behaviors including mission interruption failures, invalid actions, entering into restricted fly zones etc.
tldr: IMF is a multi-agent LLM system combining static analysis, dynamic execution, and log analysis to automatically discover logic flaws in open-source drone autopilot frameworks.
motivation: Autopilot software in autonomous drones contains subtle semantic logic flaws that are hard to detect because they span modules and rarely cause crashes or detectable failures, and LLMs alone are limited by context and training-data bias.
method: IMF uses three LLM agents: an auditor that proposes logic-flaw hypotheses via program slicing, tester agents that write and execute test cases, and a log analyzer that validates execution logs against each hypothesis, enabling case-by-case dynamic bug-oracle validation.
result: Evaluated on PX4 and ArduPilot, IMF uncovered 105 previously unknown logic flaws leading to unsafe behaviors such as mission interruption failures, invalid actions, and entrance into restricted fly zones.
conclusion: Combining LLM agents with static, dynamic, and log analysis enables automated discovery of hard-to-detect autopilot logic flaws at scale in real drone frameworks.

title: PPAD-Completeness Of Contiguous Envy-Free Cake Cutting With Additive Valuations
authors: Yasushi Kawase, Bodhayan Roy, Mohammad Azharuddin Sanpui
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that computing a complete contiguous [MATH]-envy-free cake allocation is PPAD-complete for normalized rational piecewise-constant additive valuations. The hardness holds even when [MATH] is given in unary, and even when every density takes only two values, which are the same for all agents, and is piecewise constant with at most six breakpoints. As a consequence, computing an exact contiguous envy-free allocation is also PPAD-complete, and the hardness holds under the same restrictions on the densities. Our key ingredient is to assign prices to the pieces so that, in every approximately envy-free allocation, all prices are nearly equal, regardless of how the pieces are assigned to the agents. We further show that, for every fixed integer [MATH], computing a contiguous EF[MATH] allocation of indivisible goods on a path is PPAD-complete for additive valuations, and the hardness holds even for binary valuations in which each good is valued by exactly one agent and all agents value the same number of goods.
tldr: The paper proves that computing complete contiguous envy-free cake allocations with additive valuations is PPAD-complete, even under strong restrictions on the valuation functions.
motivation: Contiguous envy-free cake cutting is a central problem in fair division, but its exact computational complexity for additive valuations remained unresolved.
method: The authors reduce from a PPAD-complete problem by assigning prices to pieces so that any approximately envy-free allocation must have nearly equal prices, and they extend the hardness to indivisible goods on a path.
result: They show PPAD-completeness for complete contiguous envy-free cake allocation with normalized rational piecewise-constant additive valuations, even when densities take only two values with at most six breakpoints, and analogous hardness for contiguous EF allocations of indivisible goods on a path.
conclusion: These results establish strong computational hardness for contiguous envy-free fair division, ruling out efficient exact algorithms unless PPAD is easy.

title: Global And Local Entropy Tests For Stl Files Under Ieee-754 Validity Constraints
authors: Borislav Stoyanov Tonislav Troev
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shannon entropy is a standard measure of ciphertext randomness, evaluated either globally over the byte histogram of the entire ciphertext or locally as the average over non-overlapping blocks of ?xed size. While the global statistic captures only the overall byte distribution, the local statistic is also sensitive to non-randomness that is con?ned to parts of the ciphertext. Both measures are commonly assessed against reference values derived under the assumption of independent uniform bytes. However, STL encodes most numerical data as single-precision IEEE-754 ?oats, and format validity requires them to be ?nite, causing nonuniform byte probabilities and dependence between the two bytes of each exponent pair. We derive the exact mean and variance of entropy under the valid-STL (VSTL) distribution, which assigns equal probability to every admissible sequence of triangle records, and provide second-order expansions that keep the global reference values practical to compute at large ?le sizes. Using these expansions, we establish a two-sided hypothesis test for the global entropy statistic, whose limiting value is lowered from 8 to 7.99991479609 bits. The format constraints also change the local entropy reference: applying the capacity energy criterion to triangle records selects a block size of 1950 bytes instead of 1936 bytes, with an exact reference mean of 7.903106732975 rather than 7.902469316647 bits. Although small, these shifts are su?cient to place the VSTL reference means outside the conventional 95% acceptance intervals at practical ?le sizes, making unadjusted entropy tests prone to falsely rejecting ideal VSTL ciphertexts. Monte-Carlo simulations con?rm all reference values within sampling error. We therefore recommend using the format-speci?c reference values derived here to evaluate STL ciphers.
tldr: Derives exact entropy reference values and hypothesis tests for STL files under IEEE-754 validity constraints, showing conventional entropy tests can falsely reject valid STL ciphertexts.
motivation: Shannon entropy tests are commonly used to assess ciphertext randomness, but STL files encode numerical data as finite IEEE-754 floats, violating the standard assumption of independent uniform bytes and leading to incorrect reference values.
method: The authors derive the exact mean and variance of global and local Shannon entropy under the valid-STL distribution, which assigns equal probability to admissible triangle records, and provide second-order expansions for practical computation at large file sizes.
result: The global entropy reference is lowered from 8 to 7.99991479609 bits, and the local entropy block size changes from 1936 to 1950 bytes with an exact mean of 7.903106732975 bits; these shifts place VSTL reference means outside conventional 95% acceptance intervals at practical file sizes, with Monte-Carlo simulations confirming the values.
conclusion: Format-specific entropy reference values should be used to evaluate STL ciphers, as unadjusted tests can falsely reject ideal VSTL ciphertexts.

title: Esau: Expeditious Swarm Remote Attestation For Pub-Sub IoT Networks With Untrusted Cloud-based Proxy Verifier
authors: Ruei-Hau Hsu, Yu-Hsiang Hu, Rafael Kaliski, Tse-Yuan Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.20047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As Internet of Things (IoT) devices collect and process data, security is essential. IoT devices often combine with other emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI) and fifth-generation (5G) communications, to support applications such as smart grids and internet-of-vehicles (IoV). Because IoT devices are deployed remotely, remote attestation (RA) effectively verifies each device's state. However, the scale of IoT deployments makes device management challenging for owners. Therefore, cloud-assisted IoT management services often provide RA solutions. Although cloud-based IoT services can securely manage IoT devices, passive malicious administrators or hacked IoT device owners' accounts can control IoT devices without cloud IoT service authorization. Therefore, this work proposes a cloud-assisted RA system that addresses three main challenges of IoT device RA: 1) lightweight RA design for resource-limited IoT devices, 2) unauthorized access to IoT devices by passive malicious administrators or compromised owner accounts on the cloud IoT management platform, and 3) RA may not extend to an authenticated key exchange protocol. In addition to proposing a swarm RA scheme that addresses these three challenges, this work analyzes the system's security properties and evaluates its feasibility through implementation and simulation.
tldr: The paper proposes Esau, a cloud-assisted remote attestation system for pub-sub IoT networks that addresses lightweight design, unauthorized cloud administrator access, and integration with authenticated key exchange.
motivation: IoT deployments are large-scale and remotely managed, making remote attestation essential, but cloud-assisted management introduces risks from passive malicious administrators or compromised owner accounts.
method: The authors design a swarm remote attestation scheme with a cloud-based proxy verifier for pub-sub IoT networks, analyze its security properties, and evaluate feasibility via implementation and simulation.
result: The proposed system tackles three key challenges: lightweight attestation for resource-constrained devices, preventing unauthorized access by untrusted cloud entities, and extending attestation to authenticated key exchange.
conclusion: Esau provides a practical and secure remote attestation solution for cloud-assisted IoT management, demonstrating feasibility for resource-limited devices in pub-sub networks.

title: Limits Of Statistical Assurance For Embodied And Agentic Ai Under Adaptive Adversaries
authors: Inderjeet Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite safety assessments cannot exclude an adversary that preserves unattacked behavior until certification and activates afterward. We characterize this limitation for embodied and tool-use AI. An adversary that matches the complete observation law until observable, irrevocable certification and retains intervention access afterward attains [MATH] expected post-certification events over [MATH] trials, where [MATH] is the active event probability and [MATH] the unattacked certification time. The result covers adaptive and privately randomized evaluators. Switching at certification is exactly optimal for a fixed likelihood-ratio test under memoryless, event-increasing interventions without a binding intervention budget. A positive clean-certification requirement forces linear worst-case expected excess when intervention raises event rates over an authorized deployment horizon, even if certification is deferred to the deadline. In simulated RoCo collaboration, switching yields commanded-separation violations in 34 of 36 post-certification episodes. Preregistered randomized AgentDojo trials estimate 1.98 additional security violations per four-task continuation (95% interval [1.67, 2.29]). An adversarial language-model controller infers hidden certification from noisy evaluation receipts and times intervention accordingly. With permanent revocation, a mixture likelihood-ratio monitor bounds cumulative excess above a prespecified reference rate at square-root order, up to logarithmic factors, on every sample path. A single fixed alternative can permit linear expected excess under stationary attacks. Against a controller observing the monitor's rule and statistic, live mixture monitoring reduces violations from 12.00 to 3.81 per 24 assigned task opportunities. Revocation also reduces tasks executed.
tldr: The paper proves fundamental limits of finite pre-deployment safety certification for embodied and agentic AI facing adaptive adversaries that switch behavior only after irrevocable certification.
motivation: Finite safety evaluations are often treated as evidence that an AI system is safe, but an adversary can in principle behave safely until certification and then activate harmful behavior afterward. This work aims to characterize the statistical limits of such certification under adaptive and randomized adversaries.
method: The authors derive worst-case bounds on post-certification events using likelihood-ratio tests and switching strategies, covering adaptive/private evaluators, and test implications in simulated RoCo collaboration and preregistered randomized AgentDojo trials with language-model adversarial controllers.
result: An optimally timing adversary can achieve expected post-certification events proportional to active probability and unattacked certification time; simulated RoCo produced commanded-separation violations in 34/36 episodes, and AgentDojo estimated 1.98 additional security violations per four-task continuation.
conclusion: Finite safety certification cannot statistically exclude adversaries that preserve clean behavior until certification and then attack; permanent revocation and live mixture monitoring can reduce but not eliminate cumulative excess violations.

title: A Unified Framework For Bell-Shaped Gaussian Quadratures In Deterministic Boltzmann Solvers
authors: Shanshan Dong, Lu Wang, Guanqing Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop a unified theoretical framework that constructs Bell-shaped Gaussian quadratures for deterministic Boltzmann solvers. The proposed framework establishes a general class of bell-shaped weight functions together with the corresponding integral transformations, revealing the common mathematical structure underlying existing generalized Gaussian quadratures. Based on this framework, a unified procedure for constructing discrete velocity sets is developed by combining radial quadratures with appropriate directional quadratures in different velocity-space dimensions. Several existing generalized Gaussian quadratures are naturally recovered as special cases, while the proposed framework provides a systematic route for constructing new quadrature rules based on different bell-shaped weight functions. Extensive benchmark simulations over a broad range of flow regimes demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves high integration accuracy and computational efficiency with significantly fewer discrete velocities than conventional quadrature strategies. Overall, the proposed framework not only unifies existing generalized Gaussian quadratures under a common mathematical foundation but also establishes a general design principle for the systematic development of efficient velocity-space quadratures in deterministic Boltzmann solvers.
tldr: The paper develops a unified framework for constructing Bell-shaped Gaussian quadratures used in deterministic Boltzmann solvers, improving velocity-space integration efficiency.
motivation: Deterministic Boltzmann solvers require efficient and accurate discrete velocity sets, but existing generalized Gaussian quadrature strategies lack a common theoretical foundation.
method: The authors introduce a general class of Bell-shaped weight functions and corresponding integral transformations, then combine radial and directional quadratures to construct discrete velocity sets.
result: The framework recovers several existing quadratures as special cases and achieves high integration accuracy with significantly fewer discrete velocities in benchmark flow simulations.
conclusion: The work unifies existing generalized Gaussian quadratures and provides a systematic design principle for efficient velocity-space quadratures in deterministic Boltzmann solvers.

title: Photoemission Study Of Iodoalkanes
authors: Maximilian Forster, Maximilian Pollanka, Sven-Joachim Paul, Pascal Freisinger, Christian Schr\"oder, Robert Richter, Michele Alagia, Alessio Bruno, Stefano Stranges, Reinhard Kienberger
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Core level atomic photoionization is influenced by the molecular environment of the emitting atom. To probe this influence we used extreme ultraviolet (XUV) radiation to measure the I[MATH] photoemission of four iodine substituted alkanes in the range from 60 eV to 160 eV photon energy. Using two detection angles relative to light polarization allowed us to extract and compare the asymmetry parameter of the investigated compounds. These results are in agreement with theory by Pi and Landsman (L.-W. Pi and A. Landsman, Attosecond time delay in photoionization of noble-gas and halogen atoms, Applied Sciences 8, 322 (2018)) and previous experiments by Olney et al. (T. N. Olney, G. Cooper, and C. Brion, Quantitative studies of the photoabsorption (4.5-488 ev) and photoionization (9-59.5 ev) of methyl iodide using dipole electron impact techniques, Chemical Physics 232, 211 (1998)) for iodomethane. 2-iodopropane behaves nearly identical to iodomethane, while for iodoethane and 1-iodopropane we find a distinct and consistent, energy dependant difference most prominent at around 130 eV photon energy. This further proves the influence of the chemical environment on core level photoionization. Due to the sensitivity on the exact positions of the carbon atoms and the energy dependence we hypothesise this difference is caused by intramolecular scattering of the outgoing photoelectron wave packet, causing changes in the angular distribution.
tldr: XUV photoemission measurements of four iodoalkanes reveal environment-dependent asymmetry parameters, attributed to intramolecular scattering of the outgoing photoelectron wave packet.
motivation: Core-level photoionization is influenced by the molecular environment, but the exact role of chemical surroundings on angular distributions remains poorly characterized.
method: The authors measured iodine 4d photoemission for four iodine-substituted alkanes from 60 to 160 eV using XUV radiation at two detection angles relative to light polarization to extract asymmetry parameters.
result: 2-iodopropane behaves nearly identically to iodomethane, while iodoethane and 1-iodopropane show a distinct energy-dependent difference, most prominent around 130 eV.
conclusion: The observed differences support the influence of the chemical environment on core-level photoionization and are hypothesized to arise from intramolecular scattering affecting the photoelectron angular distribution.

title: Wigner Time Delay In The $4d$ Giant-resonance Region Of Iodoalkanes
authors: Anatoli S. Kheifets, Daniele Toffoli, Piero Decleva
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The iodine [MATH] giant resonance provides an unusually strong and predominantly iodine-centered photoionization channel in iodoalkanes. Recent attosecond measurements by Schr\"oder et al. [Phys. Rev. A 112, L051104 (2025)] reported pronounced, nonmonotonic, and isomer-dependent variations of the streaking-derived [MATH] photoemission delay across the molecular series. We calculate field-free molecular Eisenbud--Wigner--Smith (EWS) delays from photoionization amplitudes represented in a multicenter B-spline basis of the time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT). A tensor formulation is developed in which the delay for randomly oriented molecules is evaluated from the same rank-0 and rank-2 contractions that determine the cross section and anisotropy parameter. The resulting TDDFT delays of CH[MATH]I, C[MATH]H[MATH]I, 2-iodopropane, and both calculated conformers of 1-iodopropane form a narrow bundle throughout the 90--118~eV region and closely follow atomic-I and I[MATH] reference calculations. This robustness is consistent with the similarly weak molecular dependence of the giant resonance cross section and angular distribution, but it is in marked contrast with the much larger molecular variation found by streaking experiments. The asymptotic Coulomb--laser-coupling/continuum--continuum correction is controlled mainly by the photoelectron energy and residual charge and is therefore expected to be nearly common to the iodoalkane series. This does not exclude target-specific molecular IR effects beyond the universal Coulomb term.
tldr: The paper computes field-free molecular Eisenbud-Wigner-Smith delays for photoionization of iodoalkanes in the 4d giant-resonance region using TDDFT and compares them with recent attosecond streaking experiments.
motivation: Recent attosecond measurements reported pronounced, nonmonotonic, and isomer-dependent variations of streaking-derived photoemission delays in iodoalkanes, motivating a theoretical investigation of the underlying field-free delays.
method: Photoionization amplitudes are represented in a multicenter B-spline basis with time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT), and a tensor formulation is developed to evaluate delays for randomly oriented molecules from rank-0 and rank-2 contractions.
result: The TDDFT delays for several iodoalkanes form a narrow bundle in the 90–118 eV region, closely following atomic-I and I2 reference calculations, in marked contrast with the larger molecular variation seen in streaking experiments.
conclusion: The robustness of the calculated delays is consistent with the weak molecular dependence of the giant-resonance cross section, and the discrepancy with experiments suggests that target-specific molecular IR effects beyond the universal Coulomb term may be important.

title: On The Investigation Of Antenna Beam Pattern Models For Fast Beam Placement In Leo Satellite Networks
authors: Ninh Thi-Thanh Tam, Nguyen Viet Anh, Nguyen Minh Quan, Trinh van Chien
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the impact of antenna beam pattern models on the beam placement problem in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks. Unlike conventional beam placement studies that often rely on a fixed antenna pattern or a predefined half-power beamwidth, this work compares four representative gain models, namely the Bessel [MATH] model, the combined Bessel [MATH] model, the Gaussian model, and a 3GPP-TR 37.842 model. For each antenna pattern, the corresponding half-power angle is obtained and used to construct a user compatibility graph. The beam placement problem is then transformed into a Minimum Clique Cover problem and solved using a graph coloring-based algorithm. Numerical results compare the considered antenna models in terms of the number of active beams, load balancing, statistical channel gain-to-noise ratio (SCGNR), and signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR). We analyze the impact of increasing the number of active beams on SINR-based spectral efficiency to explain the importance of carefully controlling the number of active beams. The results show that antenna beam pattern models affect both beam resource usage and link quality, highlighting the need for antenna-pattern-aware beam placement in LEO satellite networks.
tldr: The paper compares four antenna beam pattern models for beam placement in classical LEO satellite networks, formulating the problem as a minimum clique cover and analyzing trade-offs in active beams, load balancing, SCGNR, and SINR.
motivation: Beam placement in LEO satellite networks often assumes a fixed antenna pattern or half-power beamwidth, which may not reflect realistic gain models. The authors aim to quantify how different antenna pattern models affect beam resource usage and link quality.
method: For each of four gain models (Bessel, combined Bessel, Gaussian, and 3GPP-TR 37.842), the corresponding half-power angle is derived and used to build a user compatibility graph. The beam placement problem is then transformed into a Minimum Clique Cover problem and solved via a graph coloring-based algorithm.
result: Numerical comparisons show that antenna beam pattern models significantly affect the number of active beams, load balancing, statistical channel gain-to-noise ratio, and SINR. Increasing the number of active beams impacts SINR-based spectral efficiency, highlighting the need to control beam count carefully.
conclusion: Antenna-pattern-aware beam placement is important in LEO satellite networks because different pattern models lead to different beam resource usage and link quality outcomes.

title: Softplus Affine(1, 1) Processes: Enlarged Stationarity Region, Stationary Unit Roots, And Inference
authors: Fukang Zhu Yang Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Softplus affine\((1,1)\) models keep the conditional mean positive while allowing coefficients of either sign. We study them under Poisson, negative binomial, gamma and related conditional distributions. A stationary solution with moments of all positive orders exists whenever the coefficient sum is less than one, strictly enlarging previously known sufficient regions. At the unit root, the coefficient sum equals one. Under an invertibility condition, a stationary solution exists in this case if and only if the intercept is negative. At a stationary unit root, the conditional mean has a power-law tail with an explicit index, and the observations can exhibit long memory. For a fixed softplus scale, the Poisson quasi-maximum likelihood estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal at the usual \(\sqrt n\) rate below and at the unit root, with the coefficient sum left unrestricted in estimation. At the unit root, these results require only a finite mean and yield standard Wald inference even when the observations have infinite variance or long memory. Simulations and two applications examine finite-sample inference and sensitivity to the softplus scale.
tldr: The paper studies Softplus affine(1,1) time-series models with positive conditional means, weakening stationarity conditions and analyzing unit-root behavior and quasi-maximum likelihood inference.
motivation: Affine time-series models often require restrictive parameter constraints to maintain positivity and stationarity; the Softplus link is used to allow coefficients of either sign while preserving a positive conditional mean.
method: The authors derive existence conditions for stationary solutions under Poisson, negative-binomial, gamma, and related conditional distributions, analyze the unit-root case, and establish consistency and asymptotic normality of the Poisson quasi-maximum likelihood estimator.
result: They find an enlarged stationarity region when the coefficient sum is below one, characterize stationary unit roots with negative intercepts and power-law tails, and show standard Wald inference remains valid at the unit root even with infinite variance or long memory.
conclusion: Softplus affine(1,1) models provide a flexible framework for nonnegative time series with broader stationarity and tractable inference, with simulations and applications illustrating finite-sample behavior and sensitivity to the Softplus scale.

title: A Pure Source Transfer Domain Decomposition Method For Helmholtz Equations In 3d Unbounded Domain
authors: Xinran Bai, Yu Du, Haijun Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop and analyze a three-dimensional pure source transfer domain decomposition method (PSTDDM) for the Helmholtz equation in free space. Extending the two-dimensional PSTDDM proposed by [Du and Wu, J. Sci. Comput., 83(2020),83:68], the proposed method transfers sources successively along the [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH] directions, yielding layer-wise, bar-wise, and block-wise PSTDDMs. The main challenge in the convergence analysis is deriving wavenumber-explicit truncation-error estimates. To address this challenge, we establish inf--sup conditions for the uniaxial perfectly matched layer (UPML) problem under relaxed restrictions on the PML parameters and reformulate the source-transfer operators. We then introduce a positive-definite reconstruction step that produces a globally conforming approximation. In addition, a new quantitative lower bound is established for the imaginary part of the complex PML distance, more easily yielding exponential decay estimates in three dimensions. These lead to wavenumber-explicit convergence estimates for all three PSTDDMs. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods both as direct solvers and as preconditioners for GMRES.
tldr: This paper develops and analyzes a three-dimensional pure source transfer domain decomposition method (PSTDDM) for solving the Helmholtz equation in free space, with wavenumber-explicit convergence estimates.
motivation: The Helmholtz equation in unbounded 3D domains is challenging to solve numerically, and extending 2D source transfer domain decomposition methods to 3D requires new wavenumber-explicit truncation-error estimates, which are difficult to derive.
method: The authors transfer sources successively along x, y, and z directions to obtain layer-wise, bar-wise, and block-wise PSTDDMs; they establish inf-sup conditions for the uniaxial PML problem, reformulate source-transfer operators, and introduce a positive-definite reconstruction step for global conformity.
result: A new quantitative lower bound on the imaginary part of the complex PML distance yields exponential decay estimates in 3D, leading to wavenumber-explicit convergence estimates for all three PSTDDMs, validated by numerical experiments as direct solvers and GMRES preconditioners.
conclusion: The proposed 3D PSTDDM is effective both as a direct solver and as a preconditioner, with rigorous wavenumber-explicit convergence guarantees for Helmholtz problems in unbounded domains.

title: CyberArena: Benchmarking Ai Agents In Live Symmetric Attack-and-Defense Combat
authors: Bangya Liu, Jianhong Tu, Yueyang Pan, Hanhong Zhao, Zhe Ye, Hongwei Li, Saastha Vasan, Katherine Lambert, Junmin Zhu, Hao Wang, Jienan Chen, Yunze Xiao, Minglai Yang, Zihan Wang, Hairong Yin, Hao Wang, Zhiwen Fan, Tianneng Shi, Zhun Wang, Chenguang Wang, Dawn Song
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are demonstrating increasingly strong offensive and defensive cybersecurity capabilities in the real world. Current benchmarks mostly evaluate agents in isolation against static targets. Real cyber operations, however, are dynamic and coupled: security postures constantly change as attackers and defenders adapt to each other in real time. Static benchmarks quickly saturate and miss an agent's ability to attack and defend simultaneously under live pressure. To address this gap, we present CyberArena, a dynamic, symmetric adversarial benchmark built around multi-round attack-and-defense combat. In isolated sandboxes, two agents compete under identical rules, acting concurrently as both attackers and defenders over continuously changing services. This converts static targets into evolving, semi-open challenges, directly testing an agent's speed and precision in discovering, exploiting, and patching vulnerabilities. To sustain the benchmark's longevity, an automated agentic pipeline continuously generates, reviews, and validates new environments. Furthermore, because pairwise contests are notoriously hard to quantify, we introduce a dynamical model that maps match dynamics into unified, multidimensional scores across offensive, defensive, and domain-specific capabilities. Evaluating 12 frontier LLM agents across 40 challenges in 466 matches, CyberArena separates model capabilities where single-agent baselines hit a ceiling. The trajectories read like a fight rather than an exam: defenders patch one hole and miss the next and certify repairs on stale evidence, while capable agents think a move ahead, planting backdoors for later rounds and, in one case, writing their own packet sniffer to watch the opponent. Beyond a benchmark, CyberArena serves as an adaptable, scalable experimental platform for future research on cybersecurity agents.
tldr: CyberArena is a dynamic symmetric benchmark where two AI agents simultaneously attack and defend evolving services over multiple rounds.
motivation: Existing cybersecurity benchmarks evaluate AI agents in isolation against static targets, missing the dynamic and coupled nature of real attack-and-defense operations.
method: The benchmark runs multi-round combat in isolated sandboxes under identical rules, uses an automated pipeline to generate and validate new environments, and introduces a dynamical model to score offensive, defensive, and domain-specific capabilities.
result: Evaluating 12 frontier LLM agents across 40 challenges and 466 matches separated model capabilities beyond single-agent ceilings, revealing adaptive strategies such as backdoor planting and custom packet sniffers.
conclusion: CyberArena provides an adaptable, scalable experimental platform for future research on cybersecurity AI agents.

title: Majority And Torus Polynomials: Bounded-Lift Lower Bounds And Explicit Constructions
authors: Saint Wesonga
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bhrushundi et al. (2019) introduced torus polynomial approximation as an approach to separating Majority from [MATH]. In this model, approximation is measured modulo integers. Krishan and Vishwanathan (2026) developed a duality framework for lower bounds and posed five open problems. We resolve two of these, concerning integer lifts and explicit polynomial approximations. An integer lift records the integer shifts that turn a torus approximation into an ordinary real approximation. We show that a degree-d torus polynomial approximating Majority with error at most 1/8 and lift contained in an interval of width [MATH] must satisfy [MATH]. This rules out low-degree approximating polynomials with lifts in {-1, 0, 1}, answering their Open Problem 2. We also answer Open Problem 5 by giving, for every Boolean function on [MATH] variables, an explicit torus polynomial approximation of degree at most [MATH]. Its error is optimal: zero when the accepting set has even cardinality and [MATH] otherwise. The results presented were discovered and formalized in Lean using GPT-6 Astra.
tldr: The paper resolves two open problems on torus polynomial approximation of Majority and provides explicit constructions, with proofs formalized in Lean.
motivation: Torus polynomial approximation was introduced as an approach to separating Majority from ACC^0, and prior work posed open problems on integer lifts and explicit approximations.
method: The authors analyze integer lifts that convert torus approximations into ordinary real approximations, prove a lower bound on the degree for Majority, and construct explicit torus polynomials for arbitrary Boolean functions, using Lean for formalization.
result: They show that a degree-d torus polynomial approximating Majority with error ≤ 1/8 and lift width below a certain bound must have d above a threshold, ruling out low-degree lifts in {-1,0,1}. They also give an explicit approximation of degree at most some bound with optimal error: zero for even accepting sets and 1/2 otherwise.
conclusion: The work answers two of the five open problems, advances the theory of torus polynomial approximation, and demonstrates the use of Lean for formalizing complexity-theoretic results.

title: MMA-SafetyBench: A Benchmark For Multimodal Agent Safety Evaluation
authors: Yuke Wang, Benlei Cui, Shen Pang, Xuemei Dong, Longtao Huang, Hui Xue, Yuwen Zhai, Junjie Li, Jingqun Tang, Haiwen Hong
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal agents increasingly rely on visual interfaces to perceive state and select actions, creating an attack surface not captured by text-only safety evaluations. We study Visual Semantic Hijacking, in which deceptive but semantically meaningful interface elements, such as forged system alerts, cause an agent to depart from its authorized task. We propose a trajectory-guided procedure that identifies candidate injection points and inserts reproducible visual payloads into the observation stream. Using this procedure, we construct MMA-SafetyBench, which contains 1,083 adversarial trajectories across web automation, desktop GUI control, mobile navigation, document understanding, and video processing. Across nine evaluated models, Attack Success Rate (ASR) reaches 87.96%, while Semantic Compromise Rate (SCR) reaches 98.09%. A 1--3--5 scoring scheme distinguishes target-matching outputs, semantic disruption without a target match, and successful preservation of the benign task. Controls covering all nine models and five domains show that attacks persist under neutral prompts. A safety-priority prompt lowers ASR without eliminating the failure mode.
tldr: MMA-SafetyBench is a benchmark of 1,083 adversarial trajectories for evaluating the safety of multimodal LLM agents against visually injected interface attacks.
motivation: Multimodal agents increasingly act through visual interfaces, creating an attack surface that text-only safety evaluations do not capture; the authors identify 'Visual Semantic Hijacking' as an understudied threat.
method: A trajectory-guided procedure locates candidate injection points and inserts reproducible visual payloads into the agent's observation stream across web automation, desktop GUI control, mobile navigation, document understanding, and video processing domains.
result: Across nine evaluated models, attack success rate reaches 87.96% and semantic compromise rate 98.09%; controls show attacks persist under neutral prompts and a safety-priority prompt reduces but does not eliminate the failure mode.
conclusion: Multimodal agents remain highly vulnerable to visually injected semantic hijacking, motivating dedicated safety benchmarks and stronger defenses for vision-grounded agentic systems.

title: Effective-Balance Design In Ethereum Proof-of-Stake
authors: Xuechao Wang Bolin Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proof-of-Stake (PoS) systems offer a scalable and energy-efficient alternative to Proof-of-Work (PoW). The economic security of PoS relies critically on incentivizing broad and meaningful participation through well-cali\-brated staking reward mechanisms. We study Ethe\-reum's effective-balance rules as a mechanism-design problem in which the protocol chooses a reward coefficient, an activation threshold, and a maximum effective balance, and validators respond in the induced propor\-tional-allocation game. For fixed participating validators and identity counts, we establish a unique Nash equilibrium in validator-level total stakes. When validators can split or merge their visible identities, each candidate identity structure must be evaluated after the market re-clears. Restructuring incentives therefore depend on post-reset payoff comparisons that account for all validators' stake responses. For an illustrative simulation, we construct address-level budget proxies from Beacon Chain deposits and withdrawals, Lido staking flows, Etherscan balances, and calibrated synthetic agents. With illustrative cost coefficients, lowering the reserve price from 32 ETH to 30 ETH increases active identities by 5.922\% and total effective stake by 0.098\%.
tldr: The paper studies Ethereum's proof-of-stake effective-balance rules as a mechanism-design problem, analyzing validator staking incentives and identity splitting/merging.
motivation: Proof-of-stake systems need well-calibrated staking rewards to ensure economic security and broad participation, motivating a game-theoretic analysis of effective-balance parameters.
method: The authors model the protocol's reward coefficient, activation threshold, and maximum effective balance as a proportional-allocation game, establish a unique Nash equilibrium for fixed validators, and evaluate identity restructuring via post-reset payoff comparisons using illustrative simulations.
result: In an illustrative simulation with calibrated synthetic agents, lowering the reserve price from 32 ETH to 30 ETH increases active identities by 5.922% and total effective stake by 0.098%.
conclusion: The work provides a mechanism-design framework for understanding validator incentives under Ethereum's effective-balance rules, though the results are illustrative and depend on chosen cost coefficients.

title: A Non-Dichotomy For CSPs Of Stable $\omega$-Categorical Structures
authors: Manuel Bodirsky, David Bradley-Williams, Ehud Hrushovski, Christoph Spiess
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct countable, stable, [MATH]-categorical structures with at most two binary relations whose CSPs exhibit three complexity regimes: NP-complete, decidable but not in NP, and undecidable. The templates arise from a controlled Hrushovski construction of stable [MATH]-categorical graphs [MATH] for suitable irrational parameters [MATH]. Some of these graphs have NP-complete CSPs. Expanding the graphs [MATH] by the non-edge relation turns age membership into a restriction of the CSP. For every time-constructible bound [MATH], there is such an expansion whose CSP is decidable but not in DTIME[MATH]. For an explicit parameter [MATH], the restriction to complete instances belongs to [MATH] and the full CSP belongs to [MATH]. Separating the ages of the [MATH] using graphs with large girth and prescribed density yields [MATH] distinct CSPs of these expansions, all but countably many of which are undecidable.
tldr: The paper constructs stable ω-categorical structures whose constraint satisfaction problems exhibit three distinct complexity regimes, including NP-complete, decidable-but-not-in-NP, and undecidable cases.
motivation: Constraint satisfaction over infinite structures is a central topic in model theory and computational complexity, and the authors aim to show that stable ω-categorical CSPs do not obey a simple dichotomy.
method: They use a controlled Hrushovski construction to build stable ω-categorical graphs for irrational parameters, then expand these graphs by the non-edge relation to encode age membership as a CSP restriction, and separate ages using graphs with large girth and prescribed density.
result: For every time-constructible bound, there is an expansion whose CSP is decidable but not in DTIME of that bound; for an explicit parameter, the complete-instance restriction is in P and the full CSP is in NP; and they obtain continuum-many distinct CSPs, all but countably many undecidable.
conclusion: The work reveals a rich non-dichotomy in the complexity of CSPs for stable ω-categorical structures, with applications to understanding the limits of classification programs in this area.

title: Quiet Triggers, Loud Footprints: A Tri-Space Measurement Study Of Backdoor Stealthiness
authors: Behrad Tajalli, Henk Berendsen, Xiaoyun Xu, Stjepan Picek
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Backdoor attacks on deep neural networks are commonly evaluated by attack success rate and benign accuracy, yet their stealthiness remains inconsistently defined and measured. Existing work often studies only one observable aspect of stealthiness, such as trigger imperceptibility, feature-space separability, parameter-space concentration, or evasion of particular defenses. This creates a fragmented picture: an attack may appear stealthy under one metric while leaving conspicuous footprints elsewhere. This paper presents a tri-space measurement study of backdoor stealthiness in image classification. We distinguish latent stealthiness---the ideal but unobservable difficulty of distinguishing a backdoored system from a benign one---from measurable footprints in three spaces: input, feature, and parameter space. Under this framework, we evaluate representative backdoor attacks across four datasets and three model architectures using a broad suite of footprint metrics. Our results show that stealthiness is not monolithic: attacks that are quiet in one space are often loud in another, and existing attacks rarely achieve consistently small footprints across all three spaces. We further analyze agreement and disagreement among stealthiness metrics and study how footprint measurements interact with attack success rate. Based on observed blind spots in existing measurements, we introduce two diagnostic metrics: Class-Specific Davies--Bouldin Index (CDBI), which captures class-conditional feature overlap, and TAC--UCLC Product (TUP), which identifies channels that are both trigger-responsive and downstream influential. These metrics are intended to augment, not replace, the broader measurement suite. Finally, we provide practical guidance for future stealthiness evaluations.
tldr: This paper presents a tri-space measurement study of backdoor attack stealthiness in deep neural network image classifiers, distinguishing latent stealthiness from measurable footprints in input, feature, and parameter spaces.
motivation: Backdoor attack stealthiness is inconsistently defined and measured, with existing work focusing on only one observable aspect, leading to a fragmented understanding of how stealthy attacks truly are.
method: The authors evaluate representative backdoor attacks across four datasets and three architectures using a broad suite of footprint metrics, then introduce two diagnostic metrics (CDBI and TUP) to address blind spots.
result: Stealthiness is not monolithic: attacks quiet in one space are often loud in another, and existing attacks rarely achieve consistently small footprints across all three spaces; metric agreement and disagreement are analyzed.
conclusion: The paper provides practical guidance for future stealthiness evaluations and suggests that comprehensive, multi-space measurement is necessary to properly assess backdoor stealthiness.

title: Diagnose Before You Refine: Multi-Dimensional Judge Feedback For Query-Efficient Jailbreak Attacks
authors: Yixin Tan, Chia-Yi Hsu, Jiayang Liu, Chia-Mu Yu, Rui Wen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated jailbreak attacks rely on evaluation feedback to optimize adversarial prompts, but existing methods often lack fine-grained diagnostic information. We propose Jev-Guided Strategy Bandit (JSB), a query-based jailbreak framework that leverages multi-dimensional probabilistic feedback to guide prompt optimization. JSB combines continuous jailbreak scoring with targeted refinement, strategy switching, and best-state reseeding to balance exploration and refinement. We evaluate JSB on two harmful request datasets across five open-source and three closed-source LLMs. Under a budget of only 10 target-model queries, JSB achieves an average HarmBench attack success rate of 89.8\% across ten open-source settings, consistently outperforming existing automated jailbreak attacks. Further analyses demonstrate its effectiveness under varying query budgets and attacker models. Defense experiments also reveal limitations in existing filtering mechanisms and highlight the potential of Jev-based output filtering.
tldr: JSB is a query-efficient automated jailbreak framework for large language models that uses multi-dimensional probabilistic feedback to optimize adversarial prompts.
motivation: Existing automated jailbreak attacks rely on coarse evaluation feedback, limiting fine-grained diagnosis and efficient prompt refinement under tight query budgets.
method: JSB combines continuous jailbreak scoring with targeted refinement, strategy switching, and best-state reseeding to balance exploration and refinement in a bandit-style attack loop.
result: Under only 10 target-model queries, JSB achieves an average HarmBench attack success rate of 89.8% across ten open-source settings and outperforms prior automated jailbreak attacks.
conclusion: The work highlights limitations in existing filtering defenses and suggests that fine-grained diagnostic feedback can improve both jailbreak efficiency and output-filtering defenses.

title: A Direct Theory Of Strain-gradient Special Cosserat Rods Via The Principle Of Virtual Work
authors: C. Rodriguez R. S. Hallyburton
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by recent advances in the synthesis of effective one-dimensional mechanical metamaterials, we develop a direct theory of strain-gradient special Cosserat rods based on the principle of virtual work. The internal virtual work is formulated intrinsically in terms of variations of the classical Cosserat strains and their spatial derivatives, without requiring a three-dimensional parent material or a stored energy. Objectivity and insensitivity to rigid virtual displacements characterize the admissible internal-work density, while localization yields the dynamic field equations, higher-order contact interactions, natural boundary conditions, and balances of linear and angular momentum. For inextensible and unshearable rods, the constrained principle determines a unique multiplier functional, although its representation by reactive force and double-force fields possesses a gauge freedom absent from classical rod theory. We also formulate objective elastic, hyperelastic, and viscoelastic constitutive laws, extend transverse hemitropy, transverse isotropy, and flip symmetry to strain-gradient rods, and derive invariant representations of symmetric stored energies. As an application, we study a planar inextensible cantilever under a compressive terminal force. We prove that the eigenvalues of the linearized problem are simple and coincide precisely with the loads at which bifurcation from the straight state occurs. In addition, each bifurcation point generates a connected global branch of nonlinear equilibria that is locally analytic near its origin.
tldr: The paper develops a direct theory of strain-gradient special Cosserat rods using the principle of virtual work, without reference to a 3D parent material.
motivation: Recent advances in synthesizing effective one-dimensional mechanical metamaterials motivate a need for a direct rod theory that incorporates strain-gradient effects.
method: The internal virtual work is formulated intrinsically in terms of variations of classical Cosserat strains and their spatial derivatives, leading to dynamic field equations, higher-order contact interactions, and natural boundary conditions via localization.
result: The theory yields a unique multiplier functional for constrained rods, objective constitutive laws, invariant representations of stored energies, and a proof that linearized eigenvalues coincide with bifurcation loads for a planar inextensible cantilever.
conclusion: The framework provides a comprehensive strain-gradient rod theory with gauge freedom in reactive fields and extends symmetry concepts, enabling analysis of nonlinear equilibria and bifurcations.

title: A Finite Coefficient Theory For Shape Identification In Tilted Generalized Gamma Families
authors: Ran Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A continuous shape parameter enters both a radial density and the normalization of its transform coefficients. This coupling allows changes in shape to be compensated by changes in scale and exponential tilt. We study the coefficients b_k=e^a E[Y^k ]/[k!(d)_k ] for densities proportional to y^(d-1) exp(-{\alpha}y^q+y), with known integer q>=2, d,{\alpha}>0, and unrestricted real a,. For q=2, the first four coefficients determine all parameters globally, whereas three coefficients leave an analytic curve of solutions. We characterize the exact image of the two shape ratios and prove that two alternating corners decide whether an entire coefficient box is realizable and give its exact shape range. For every fixed q, the first q(q+1) coefficients give global identification and an everywhere full-rank map. A finite-difference criterion yields generic identification from 2q+1 coefficients, including every zero-tilt model against the full tilted family. For q=3, an exact rational certificate constructs two distinct shapes with identical first four coefficients and separated fifth coefficients. The results distinguish exact identification, realizability, and sensitivity for a parameter-dependent coefficient normalization.
tldr: This paper develops a finite coefficient theory for identifying shape parameters in tilted generalized gamma families, using moment-like coefficients to characterize exact and generic parameter identifiability.
motivation: The author aims to understand how continuous shape parameters coupled with scale and exponential tilt affect the identifiability of probability densities from a finite number of transform coefficients.
method: The analysis studies coefficients b_k = e^a E[Y^k]/[k!(d)_k] for densities proportional to y^{d-1} exp(-α y^q + y), deriving conditions for global identification, realizability of coefficient boxes, and finite-difference identification criteria.
result: For q=2, the first four coefficients determine all parameters globally while three leave a curve of solutions; for general q, the first q(q+1) coefficients give global identification, and a fifth coefficient separates shapes when q=3.
conclusion: The work distinguishes exact identification, realizability, and sensitivity in a parameter-dependent coefficient normalization, providing a finite-coefficient framework for shape identification in tilted generalized gamma families.

title: Neural Spline Flow Diffeomorphisms For Pullback Finite Element Methods On Complex Domains
authors: Ioannis Kalogeris, Anaksagoras Spitas, Konstantinos Atzarakis, George Stavroulakis, Vissarion Papadopoulos
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a method for solving partial differential equations on complex domains by learning smooth, invertible mappings from a fixed reference domain using Neural Spline Flows (NSFs). Monotone rational-quadratic spline coupling layers ensure a strictly positive Jacobian determinant by construction, eliminating the need for Jacobian-sign penalties. A diffeomorphic pullback transfers the weak form of the PDE to the reference domain, enabling finite element analysis on reusable structured meshes. To generalize across shapes, a shared NSF is conditioned on low-dimensional latent codes learned through an auto-decoder framework; a subsequent encoder predicts these codes for unseen geometries in a single forward pass. For a given learned map, the pullback preserves the mathematical structure of the PDE and is exactly equivalent to solving on the domain represented by that map. Because the learned domain generally approximates the target geometry, geometric mapping error remains distinct from finite element discretization and quadrature errors. Numerical benchmarks show that sufficiently accurate learned mappings yield reliable finite element solutions. By avoiding repeated generation of unstructured meshes, the method addresses a bottleneck in simulation workflows. The fixed reference mesh also creates opportunities for efficient assembly, memory-aligned data access, and precomputed quadrature. The resulting framework assigns geometric complexity to the neural network while retaining conventional finite element discretization and convergence properties on the learned domain, with overall accuracy also governed by geometric fidelity.
tldr: The paper proposes learning diffeomorphic mappings from a reference domain to complex geometries using Neural Spline Flows, enabling pullback finite element analysis on reusable structured meshes.
motivation: Solving PDEs on complex domains typically requires repeated generation of unstructured meshes, which is a bottleneck in simulation workflows.
method: Monotone rational-quadratic spline coupling layers in a Neural Spline Flow guarantee a positive Jacobian determinant by construction, and a diffeomorphic pullback transfers the PDE weak form to a fixed reference domain; a shared flow conditioned on auto-decoder latent codes generalizes across shapes.
result: Numerical benchmarks show that sufficiently accurate learned mappings yield reliable finite element solutions, with geometric mapping error distinct from discretization and quadrature errors.
conclusion: The framework assigns geometric complexity to the neural network while preserving conventional finite element discretization and convergence properties, enabling efficient assembly, memory-aligned data access, and precomputed quadrature.

title: On Local Inference For Functionals Of Ill-Posed Inverse Problems
authors: Andrea Rotnitzky Ellen Graham
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study inference for continuous linear functionals of solutions to ill-posed inverse problems, including Euclidean parameters arising in nonparametric instrumental variables, proximal causal inference, and shadow-variable models. Although pointwise root-[MATH] inference is possible under standard conditions, we show that this need not translate into locally reliable inference. Under a model imposing only minimal regularity conditions, the target is Hellinger discontinuous when both inverse problems are ill-posed: arbitrarily small changes in the data-generating law can produce arbitrarily large changes in the target, ruling out informative locally uniform inference. Imposing a uniform bound on a minimum-norm solution restores Hellinger continuity under regularity conditions, but does not by itself ensure stable root-n inference. If, in addition, both inverse problems are ill-posed and the solution whose norm is uniformly bounded is nonunique at a law [MATH], then under regularity conditions the target fails to be pathwise differentiable; consequently, asymptotically linear estimators exhibit nonvanishing root-[MATH] bias under some local alternatives, causing Wald confidence intervals to undercover asymptotically. Under regularity conditions, pathwise differentiability is restored if the uniformly bounded solution is unique at [MATH]. It is also restored, regardless of uniqueness, under the stronger requirement that the corresponding solution satisfy a uniformly bounded [MATH]-source condition for some [MATH]>0. We relate these regimes to very weak, weak, and strong identification in instrumental variables models.
tldr: The paper studies inference for continuous linear functionals of solutions to ill-posed inverse problems, showing that root-n pointwise inference can fail to yield locally reliable inference due to Hellinger discontinuity and pathwise non-differentiability.
motivation: Inference for functionals of ill-posed inverse problems is important in nonparametric instrumental variables, proximal causal inference, and shadow-variable models, but standard root-n rates may not guarantee stable local inference.
method: The authors analyze Hellinger continuity and pathwise differentiability under minimal regularity conditions, considering regimes with ill-posed inverse problems, bounds on minimum-norm solutions, and uniqueness or source conditions.
result: They show that with both inverse problems ill-posed, the target can be Hellinger discontinuous; a uniform bound restores continuity but not stable root-n inference, and nonuniqueness can break pathwise differentiability, causing asymptotically linear estimators to have nonvanishing bias and Wald intervals to undercover.
conclusion: Reliable locally uniform inference requires additional conditions such as uniqueness of the bounded solution or a uniformly bounded source condition, with connections to weak and strong identification in instrumental variables models.

title: A Potential Projection Method For The Nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger Equation With Low Regularity Potential
authors: Weizhu Bao, Qingyuan Sun, Chushan Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a potential projection (PP) method for the nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation (NLSE) with low-regularity and singular potentials by replacing the potential with its Fourier projection (truncated Fourier series). This gives rise to an NLSE with projected potential (NLSEwPP). We rigorously establish its well-posedness under low-regularity potentials, and its convergence to the original NLSE. The NLSEwPP is then directly discretized by the standard time-splitting Fourier pseudospectral (TS-FP) method with the mesh size chosen according to the potential projection parameter, resulting in the fully discrete TS-PP-FP method. Numerically, TS-PP-FP consistently achieves optimal temporal and spatial convergence rates with respect to the regularity of the exact solution under low-regularity and even singular potentials. Compared with the time-splitting Fourier spectral method, TS-PP-FP attains the same convergence rates at significantly lower computational cost and preserves the mass conservation and time symmetry (that are lost in the Fourier spectral discretization of the time-splitting method); compared with the time-splitting FP method, it is substantially more accurate for low-regularity potentials with the same computational cost.
tldr: The paper proposes a potential projection method for numerically solving the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with low-regularity or singular potentials, using Fourier projection and time-splitting pseudospectral discretization.
motivation: Standard time-splitting Fourier pseudospectral methods lose accuracy for low-regularity potentials and can fail to preserve mass conservation and time symmetry.
method: The authors replace the potential by its truncated Fourier series, prove well-posedness and convergence of the resulting projected-potential NLSE, and discretize it with a time-splitting Fourier pseudospectral scheme.
result: The fully discrete TS-PP-FP method achieves optimal temporal and spatial convergence rates under low-regularity potentials, preserves mass and time symmetry, and is more accurate or cheaper than competing Fourier spectral methods.
conclusion: The potential projection technique provides an efficient and robust numerical framework for NLSE with singular or low-regularity potentials, though it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Large-Step Last-Iterate Convergence Of Random-Reshuffling Stochastic Gradient Descent
authors: Zihan Zhang Zijun Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Random reshuffling stochastic gradient descent (RR-SGD) is widely used for finite-sum optimization in machine learning. For convex [MATH]-smooth components, recent work establishes convergence guarantees for an averaged iterate with component stepsizes as large as order [MATH]. However, the final iterate is a natural output in practice, and existing last-iterate guarantees in this setting require stepsizes that scale inversely with the number of components [MATH]. We establish an expected objective-gap bound for the last iterate of standard RR-SGD on unconstrained problems with a constant component stepsize satisfying [MATH], where [MATH] is the number of epochs. By retaining the sampling bias at random comparison points, we remove the explicit [MATH] factor from the stepsize restriction. Combined with existing small-step bounds, our result matches the corresponding averaged-iterate convergence rate up to logarithmic factors.
tldr: The paper establishes last-iterate convergence guarantees for random-reshuffling stochastic gradient descent with large constant component stepsizes.
motivation: RR-SGD is widely used for finite-sum optimization, but existing last-iterate guarantees require very small stepsizes, unlike practical implementations and averaged-iterate theory.
method: The authors analyze the last iterate of standard RR-SGD for convex smooth finite-sum problems, retaining sampling bias at random comparison points to avoid an explicit dependence on the number of components.
result: They prove an expected objective-gap bound for constant component stepsizes of order O(1/sqrt(n)) up to logarithmic factors, matching averaged-iterate rates and removing the small-step restriction.
conclusion: Large-step last-iterate convergence is achievable for RR-SGD, bringing theoretical guarantees closer to practical usage.

title: Digital Self-Interference Cancellation For In-Band Full-Duplex Systems Based On Transformer Neural Operators
authors: Zhijie Su, Shiquan Zhang, Qiaolin He
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Digital-domain self-interference cancellation is essential in in-band full-duplex radios after passive suppression and analog cancellation. It is particularly challenging when the desired signal is strong relative to the residual self-interference. In this regime, conventional iterative digital cancellers update their coefficients from desired-signal-contaminated received samples and may suffer substantial performance degradation. This paper reformulates digital-domain self-interference cancellation as an operator-learning problem. The proposed framework learns the temporal evolution of the residual self-interference channel from historical observations and uses the learned operator together with the known local transmit signal to reconstruct the current residual self-interference. A Transformer neural operator is used to realize this framework. The resulting method is trained in a desired-signal-free setting and then applied in the presence of a desired signal. A continuity-based analysis characterizes the sensitivity of the learned operator to the resulting input perturbation. Numerical experiments in static and time-varying channels, including time-varying SIR conditions, demonstrate stable cancellation performance over a wide range of interference levels. At 30 dB SIR, the proposed method improves the cancellation performance by 5--15 dB over the considered conventional methods.
tldr: A Transformer neural operator framework is proposed for digital self-interference cancellation in in-band full-duplex systems.
motivation: Digital-domain self-interference cancellation is difficult when the desired signal is strong relative to residual self-interference, causing conventional iterative cancellers to degrade.
method: The paper reformulates digital self-interference cancellation as an operator-learning problem and uses a Transformer neural operator to learn the temporal evolution of the residual self-interference channel from historical observations, trained in a desired-signal-free setting.
result: Numerical experiments show stable cancellation across static and time-varying channels, with 5–15 dB improvement over conventional methods at 30 dB SIR.
conclusion: The proposed operator-learning approach improves digital self-interference cancellation, but the work lies in classical communication signal processing and is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: AutoPoly-HE: Autonomous Design Of Polynomial Activations For Privacy-Preserving Encrypted Inference
authors: Zeinab Elkhatib, Kamrul Hasan, Ali Sekmen, Imtiaz Ahmed, Tariqul Islam
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Privacy-preserving machine learning has become critical for deploying artificial intelligence in sensitive domains such as healthcare, finance, and infrastructure monitoring. Homomorphic encryption (HE) enables secure inference on encrypted data. Despite its advantages, HE is not compatible with nonlinear activation functions found in machine learning models. Existing methods mitigate this problem by manually designing polynomial approximations for these activation functions. However, these functions do not account for the differences in dataset characteristics or model architecture. Furthermore, these functions are also limited to the accuracies of convolutional neural network (CNN) models. In this work, we propose an autonomous framework that selects polynomial activation functions tailored to each dataset and model. Using this framework, we analyze the interdependence between polynomial activation design and model architecture by evaluating several CNN ResNet and Vision Transformer models across multiple datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework generalizes across multiple architectures, including ResNet-18, ResNet-34, ResNet-50, ViT-S/16, ViT-B/16, and ViT-L/16. Across all datasets, transformer-based models maintain higher accuracy under polynomial approximation, while convolutional models exhibit increased degradation as task complexity grows. In addition, latency analysis reveals that the proposed CLS token based inference pipeline significantly reduces computational overhead by eliminating depth-dependent operations, shifting the primary cost to encryption and decryption. These findings demonstrate that the proposed method not only adapts polynomial activations across architectures, but also enables efficientencrypted inference through both activation design and pipeline optimization.
tldr: The paper proposes an autonomous framework for selecting polynomial activation functions to enable privacy-preserving encrypted inference with homomorphic encryption across CNN and Vision Transformer models.
motivation: Homomorphic encryption enables secure inference on encrypted data but is incompatible with standard nonlinear activations, and existing polynomial approximations are manually designed and fail to adapt to dataset or model architecture.
method: The authors develop an autonomous pipeline that selects polynomial activation functions tailored to each dataset and model, and evaluate ResNet and ViT architectures on multiple datasets with latency analysis of a CLS-token-based inference pipeline.
result: Transformer models maintain higher accuracy under polynomial approximation, while convolutional models degrade more as task complexity increases; the CLS-token pipeline reduces depth-dependent overhead, shifting cost to encryption and decryption.
conclusion: The framework generalizes across architectures and enables efficient encrypted inference by jointly optimizing activation design and inference pipeline.

title: What You Sign Is Not What You Run: The Verifiability Gap In Quantized Llm Supply Chains
authors: Cheng-Yen Tsai Wei-Liang Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model signing authenticates the full-precision weights W an LLM is released with, yet users run a quantized artifact Q whose producing transformation is not uniquely determined under current disclosure. We separate the non-environment inputs from the execution environment E and measure a quantity that, to our knowledge, has not been measured before: the Independent Verifiability Rate (IVR), the fraction of a popularity-sampled GGUF ecosystem that a third party can re-derive bit-for-bit. Across the 200 most-downloaded Hugging Face GGUF repositories (198 in scope), no artifact or model card records the build environment, so under a recorded-inputs protocol the IVR is 0/198. Yet the artifacts are not irreproducible. On four in-sample repositories that disclose their inputs, the card's information alone reproduces no Q4_K_M file, but two coordinates the card omits - the build's floating-point-contraction setting and, for hybrid models, the per-tensor quantization recipe - re-derive 7/8 target-quant files bit-for-bit on x86 (5/8 on arm64); the fp16 re-derives from the provider's checkpoint, but the calibration imatrix must be shipped and hash-bound, since recomputing it did not match. An older release additionally pins the instruction set and did not re-derive. Reproducing the divergence reported with llama.cpp PR #25353, we show that E is a necessary coordinate and that one compiler setting yields a unique output across the tested platforms at negligible quality cost (+0.06% perplexity). As a security characterization, benign floating-point non-determinism separates from uniformly placed nibble-flip tampering above a detection floor that grows with the environments a verifier must allow, but a targeted embedding edit evades the statistic, so the proposed protocol rests on exact re-derivation; adversarial-fp16 attacks lie outside it. We release the audit data and a re-runnable harness.
tldr: The paper identifies a verifiability gap in quantized LLM supply chains, showing that signed full-precision weights do not guarantee the quantized artifact users actually run can be independently reproduced.
motivation: Model signing authenticates released weights, but users run quantized artifacts whose producing transformations are not uniquely determined under current disclosure, raising supply-chain security concerns.
method: The authors define the Independent Verifiability Rate (IVR) and audit the 200 most-downloaded Hugging Face GGUF repositories, testing whether model-card information plus omitted build coordinates can re-derive quantized files bit-for-bit.
result: Under a recorded-inputs protocol the IVR is 0/198; adding the floating-point-contraction setting and per-tensor quantization recipe re-derives 7/8 target files on x86 and 5/8 on arm64. Benign non-determinism is separable from nibble-flip tampering above a detection floor, but targeted embedding edits evade the statistic.
conclusion: Verification of quantized LLM artifacts requires exact re-derivation protocols rather than current model signing alone; the audit data and a re-runnable harness are released. This work is outside quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Femtosecond All-optical Polarization Manipulation Of Harmonic Generation In An Anisotropic Strongly Coupled Plasmon-epsilon-near-zero Metasurface
authors: Yingying Zhang, Jinhai Si, Xun Hou, Kuidong Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultrafast manipulation of light polarization plays a key role in modern high-speed photonics and optoelectronic operations. However, most current polarization-active modulation schemes are restricted by a limited operating wavelength range (visible to infrared), narrow-band resonant fundamental wavelength working condition, and relatively long modulation time (> 1 picosecond). Here, by taking advantage of the transient anisotropic nonlinearity of optical strong coupling between the epsilon-near-zero mode of indium tin oxide (ITO) film and polarization-selective plasmonic resonance, we achieve femtosecond polarization manipulation of broadband light that spans ultraviolet (UV) to visible region by controlling harmonic generation of the signal light under resonant pumping. We demonstrate polarization elliptic rotation of 23.3{\deg} at 407 nm for third-harmonic generation (THG) and 55.0{\deg} at 610 nm for second-harmonic generation (SHG) simultaneously within ~600 fs. In addition, the strongly coupled system can also serve as a universal femtosecond polarization modulation source, imprinting a 32.9{\deg} polarization rotation in the UV region by converting the modulation information of the fundamental signal light to that of THG light via a uniform ITO film in a cascaded configuration. Our study establishes a new paradigm for UV-based, ultrahigh-speed broadband polarization photonics with direct implications for high-speed optical information processing and programmable nonlinear photonic devices.
