tldr: Demonstrates femtosecond all-optical polarization manipulation of second- and third-harmonic generation in a plasmon-epsilon-near-zero metasurface via anisotropic strong coupling.
motivation: Current polarization-active modulators are limited by narrow operating wavelength ranges and picosecond-scale response times, hindering high-speed broadband photonic applications.
method: Exploits transient anisotropic nonlinearity from strong coupling between the epsilon-near-zero mode of an ITO film and polarization-selective plasmonic resonance to control harmonic generation under resonant pumping.
result: Achieves polarization elliptic rotation of 23.3° at 407 nm for THG and 55.0° at 610 nm for SHG simultaneously within ~600 fs, plus 32.9° UV rotation in a cascaded ITO configuration.
conclusion: Establishes a platform for UV-based, ultrahigh-speed broadband polarization photonics with potential for high-speed optical information processing and programmable nonlinear devices.

title: Right Coideal Subalgebras, Hopf Galois Objects, And $\imath$-Hopf Algebras
authors: Rongchuan Xiong
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study right comodule algebras and their connections with Hopf bi-Galois objects and right coideal subalgebras. For a Hopf [MATH]-cocycle [MATH] on [MATH] and a unital right-colinear algebra map [MATH], we show that [MATH] is an algebra map precisely when [MATH] is trivial on [MATH]. We describe comodule-algebra morphisms [MATH] by characters and establish injectivity criteria using the coradical and extensions of characters to convolution-invertible functionals. For coactions on Hopf quotients projecting to the coproduct, character-evaluation maps are injective, and equality of their images is determined by a unique algebra character. For the [MATH]-Hopf algebras [MATH] of Chen--Lu--Pan--Ruan--Wang, with [MATH] having a bijective antipode and a Hopf pairing, we obtain a Hopf bi-Galois realization [MATH]. We identify algebra characters with nonzero [MATH]-twisted compatible maps [MATH] and prove that the corresponding morphisms [MATH] of Chen--Lu--Pan--Ruan--Wang are injective, yielding right coideal realizations in [MATH]. We classify the [MATH] up to comodule-algebra isomorphism and determine when these realizations have the same image.
tldr: This paper studies right comodule algebras, Hopf bi-Galois objects, and right coideal subalgebras, with applications to i-Hopf algebras.
motivation: The work aims to clarify algebraic structures and morphisms between comodule algebras and coideal subalgebras in the context of Hopf algebra theory.
method: The authors use Hopf algebra techniques including Hopf cocycles, characters, coradicals, and convolution-invertible functionals to analyze injectivity and classify structures.
result: They obtain a Hopf bi-Galois realization for certain i-Hopf algebras, identify algebra characters with twisted compatible maps, and classify coideal realizations up to isomorphism.
conclusion: The paper advances the algebraic theory of coideal subalgebras and Galois objects but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: The Two-Level Poset Game Is PSPACE-Complete
authors: Kengo Hashimoto
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Poset games form a fundamental class of combinatorial games that includes classical games such as Nim and Chomp. Determining the outcome of a poset game is known to be PSPACE-complete even for posets of height at most three. However, the exact computational complexity of Two-Level Poset Game, played on posets of height at most two, has remained an open problem for over a decade. We resolve this problem by proving that Two-Level Poset Game is PSPACE-complete via a polynomial-time reduction from Avoid True on positive CNF formulas.
tldr: The paper proves that the Two-Level Poset Game, played on posets of height at most two, is PSPACE-complete, resolving a decade-old open problem in combinatorial game complexity.
motivation: Poset games generalize classical games like Nim and Chomp, and while PSPACE-completeness was known for height-three posets, the complexity of the height-two (two-level) case had remained open for over ten years.
method: The author constructs a polynomial-time reduction from the game Avoid True on positive CNF formulas to the Two-Level Poset Game, thereby transferring PSPACE-hardness to the two-level setting.
result: Two-Level Poset Game is shown to be PSPACE-complete, closing the gap between the trivially solvable height-one case and the previously established height-three hardness.
conclusion: The result fully characterizes the computational complexity of poset games by height, with the height-two case now proven intractable unless PSPACE collapses.

title: Standardized Planck-Mean Absorption Coefficients For High-Temperature Gases
authors: Ryan D. Deboskey, Clayton M. Geipel, Brian T. Bojko
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Planck-mean absorption coefficients of pure gases are calculated from line-by-line integrations of HITEMP and ExoMol spectra up to 5000 K for use in high-enthalpy radiative heat transfer simulations. The dataset extends beyond conventional combustion products, including high-temperature radicals, nitrogen-bearing species, soot precursors, metal oxides, metal hydrides, and halides: AlF, AlH, AlO, BH, C2, C2H2, CH, CH4, CN, CO, CO2, H2O, HBO, HCN, HF, MgH, MgO, N2O, NO, NO2, OH, SiO, TiH, TiO. New calculations are validated against historical correlations for overlapping species, demonstrating good agreement over their applicable temperature ranges. Strong visible opacities result in large Planck-mean absorption coefficients for many of the considered species, highlighting the need to account for their radiative contribution in extreme environments. A brute-force search over several candidate functional forms is performed to provide a common set of coefficients, establishing a standardized framework that can be easily integrated into production solvers and extended as additional high-temperature line lists become available.
tldr: The paper computes standardized Planck-mean absorption coefficients for high-temperature gases from HITEMP and ExoMol line lists up to 5000 K for radiative heat transfer simulations.
motivation: High-enthalpy radiative heat transfer simulations require accurate absorption coefficients for many high-temperature species beyond conventional combustion products.
method: Line-by-line integrations of HITEMP and ExoMol spectra were performed for 24 species, validated against historical correlations, and a brute-force search was used to find a common functional form.
result: Many species exhibit strong visible opacities and large Planck-mean absorption coefficients, and a standardized coefficient framework is provided for production solvers.
conclusion: The dataset enables inclusion of high-temperature radiative contributions and can be extended as additional line lists become available.

title: The Gompertz-Zipf City Size Distribution And Urban Allometry
authors: Sharon Teles
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This dissertation discusses the distribution of city sizes using censuses of the Brazilian Institute for Geography and Statistics (IBGE) spanning 150 years, from 1872 to 2022, as well as the allometric scaling relation with the 2022 census data. The Gompertz distribution is fitted to the population size of less populated cities, while the Zipf power law is used to represent the cities having larger populations, with threshold varying between 20,216 and 102,857 inhabitants. The data analysis shows that the Gompertz-Zipf distribution can describe the data across all censuses, with the Gompertz parameter [MATH] oscillating between [MATH] and [MATH], indicating periods with faster decreases and periods with slower decreases in the number of cities within the less populated segment as population increases, while the Zipf exponent ranges from [MATH] in 1872 to [MATH] in 2022. The Gini coefficient [MATH] and the Zanardi index [MATH] are used to quantify the inequality in the city population distribution, whose obtained values are [MATH] and [MATH] for the 1872 census and [MATH] and [MATH] for the 2022 dataset, while the Pietra index [MATH] and the Kolkata index [MATH], associated with the most populated cities, are [MATH] and [MATH] for 1872, and [MATH] and [MATH] for 2022. These results reveal a high concentration of population in larger cities, with [MATH] increasing from 1872 to 2022 and [MATH] becoming positive after 1900, indicating a greater concentration of population in the group of more populated cities than in the group of less populated cities. Finally, urban allometry is also examined, generating an exponent [MATH] for the 2022 data, showing that the scaling relation between area and population holds for urbanized area but not for total administrative area, indicating that scaling is associated with spatial occupation.
tldr: This dissertation analyzes 150 years of Brazilian census data to model city size distributions using a Gompertz-Zipf combination and examines urban allometric scaling.
motivation: The paper aims to characterize the statistical distribution of city sizes over time and to test whether urban area scales with population, addressing questions in urban economics and geography.
method: The authors fit a Gompertz distribution to smaller cities and a Zipf power law to larger cities, with a variable threshold, and compute inequality indices (Gini, Zanardi, Pietra, Kolkata) and allometric scaling exponents.
result: The Gompertz-Zipf distribution describes all censuses, with the Zipf exponent decreasing from 1872 to 2022, inequality indices rising over time, and the allometric exponent showing scaling for urbanized area but not total administrative area.
conclusion: Population is increasingly concentrated in larger cities, and urban scaling is associated with spatial occupation rather than administrative boundaries.

title: A Nonequilibrium-capturing Unified Gas-kinetic Scheme I: Discrete Orthogonal Basis Construction And Expansion On Velocity Space
authors: Kun Xu Hongyu Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Velocity space discretization is a primary source of computational cost in deterministic methods for multiscale gas flows. A fixed velocity grid often retains redundant kinetic degrees of freedom (DOFs), particularly under near equilibrium conditions. To address this issue, this work develops a nonequilibrium-capturing formulation based on the unified gas kinetic scheme (UGKS), in which the number of kinetic DOFs adapts locally to the degree of nonequilibrium. A discrete orthogonal basis is constructed for numerical implementation, and the velocity distribution function is decomposed into an analytical local equilibrium and a basis expanded nonequilibrium component. The retained, locally adapted DOFs are evolved directly, substantially lowering computational overhead while preserving the discrete conservation of mass, momentum, and energy, as well as accurately capturing nonequilibrium states. The formulation retains the core multiscale coupling of molecular transport and collision inherent to UGKS, providing explicit and implicit schemes for unsteady and steady flows, respectively. Numerical tests across a wide range of flow speeds and rarefaction regimes (from continuum to highly rarefied) demonstrate close agreement with benchmark solutions. For unsteady flows, the explicit scheme achieves speedups of 12.64 to 58.50 over the standard UGKS. In steady state tests, only about [MATH] of the original kinetic DOFs are required in continuum regions, accelerating each implicit iteration by a factor of 33.87. Even in the most rarefied cases, the scheme captures nonequilibrium behavior using only about [MATH] of the original DOFs.
tldr: A new numerical scheme reduces kinetic degrees of freedom in the unified gas-kinetic scheme by adaptively capturing nonequilibrium, achieving significant speedups.
motivation: Velocity space discretization in deterministic methods for multiscale gas flows often retains redundant kinetic degrees of freedom, especially near equilibrium, leading to high computational cost.
method: The authors construct a discrete orthogonal basis and decompose the velocity distribution function into an analytical local equilibrium and a basis-expanded nonequilibrium component, evolving only locally adapted degrees of freedom while preserving conservation laws.
result: Numerical tests show speedups of 12.64 to 58.50 for unsteady flows and up to 33.87 per implicit iteration for steady flows, using only a fraction of the original DOFs even in rarefied cases, while matching benchmark solutions.
conclusion: The nonequilibrium-capturing UGKS formulation substantially reduces computational overhead while accurately capturing nonequilibrium states, enabling efficient simulation of multiscale gas flows.

title: On The Nonnegative Integer Solutions To The Equation $F_n^2+F_m=2^{a}$
authors: Sagar Mandal
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Diophantine equation [MATH] where [MATH] denotes the [MATH]-th Fibonacci number and [MATH], has attracted attention in recent years. The cases [MATH] and [MATH] were completely resolved by Bravo and Luca, and by Jeong and Park, respectively. In this note, we investigate the mixed exponent case [MATH] and we completely determine all nonnegative integer solutions.
tldr: This paper completely determines all nonnegative integer solutions to the Diophantine equation F_n^2 + F_m = 2^a in the mixed exponent case.
motivation: The equation has attracted recent attention, with the cases previously resolved by Bravo and Luca and by Jeong and Park, but the mixed exponent case remained open.
method: The author uses number-theoretic techniques for Fibonacci Diophantine equations, including modular arithmetic, bounds, and classical results on Fibonacci numbers.
result: All nonnegative integer solutions to the mixed exponent case are completely determined.
conclusion: The paper extends prior work and completes the solution of the equation for the remaining mixed exponent case.

title: Adjoint Transfer And Order-Lifting Dichotomies For 2 X 2 Matrices Over Prime-Power Rings
authors: Ivo Vajc
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an odd prime p, we study the change in matrix order under lifting from Z/p^k Z to Z/p^(k+1) Z. The first variation of the order defect is an affine translate of a cyclic adjoint transfer on sl_2(F_p). We classify the full-order transfer for every q in GL_2(F_p): its rank is 3 for scalar elements, 1 for nonscalar semisimple elements, 1 for nonscalar Jordan elements when p = 3, and 0 for nonscalar Jordan elements when p > 3. For a Jordan element q = lambda(I + U), U^2 = 0 and U != 0, the vanishing first-order transfer for p > 3 admits an exact higher-order refinement. Writing d = (p - 1)/2, the full-order perturbation has depth d when tr(UX) != 0, depth p - 1 when tr(UX) = 0 and X is not in the span of U, and vanishes identically for X in the span of U. For p = 3, among the 27 lifts of a nonscalar order-preserving parent with determinant fixed to +1 or -1, exactly 9 preserve its order and 18 triple it; after the first increase, every further lift triples the order. We also give a scalar obstruction criterion for order preservation among unrestricted Jordan lifts.
tldr: The paper classifies how matrix order changes under lifting 2x2 matrices from Z/p^kZ to Z/p^(k+1)Z, using adjoint transfer on sl_2(F_p).
motivation: The authors aim to understand order-lifting phenomena for matrices over prime-power rings and to provide a complete first-order and higher-order analysis of order defects under such lifts.
method: They study the change in matrix order via an adjoint transfer map on sl_2(F_p), classify its rank for different elements of GL_2(F_p), and analyze higher-order refinements for Jordan elements, including explicit counts for p=3.
result: The full-order transfer has rank 3 for scalars, rank 1 for nonscalar semisimple elements, rank 1 for nonscalar Jordan elements when p=3, and rank 0 for nonscalar Jordan elements when p>3; for p>3, the higher-order perturbation has depth depending on tr(UX).
conclusion: The paper provides a detailed algebraic classification of order lifting for 2x2 matrices over prime-power rings, including a scalar obstruction criterion for order preservation among Jordan lifts.

title: A Multipatch Model For Evaluating Interdivisional Connectivity And Vaccination Dynamics In The 2026 Bangladesh Measles Outbreak
authors: Md. Kamrujjaman Faizunnesa Khondaker
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The 2026 measles resurgence in Bangladesh motivates a spatial modelling framework that accounts for heterogeneous local transmission, vaccination activity, and interdivisional connectivity. We formulate a multipatch susceptible-vaccinated-infectious-recovered model for the eight administrative divisions of Bangladesh. Division-specific parameters are estimated from reported measles cases and smoothed vaccination data using bounded nonlinear least squares, with uncertainty quantified through 1000 parametric bootstrap replicates. The fitted divisional systems are then connected through compartment-specific movement and cross-patch infection coefficients adjusted for connectivity and the source division's relative reproduction number. The fitted model captures the main division-specific epidemic patterns. Estimated local reproduction numbers range from \(1.1386\) in Khulna (95\% CI:\(0.5703\)--\(1.3834\)) to \(4.3491\) in Dhaka (95\% CI: \(1.4449\)--\(5.6307\)), while Chattogram also exhibits high transmission potential (\(_0^i=4.2275\); 95\% CI: \(4.0019\)--\(4.3185\)). Baseline spatial coupling increases the network-wide epidemic peak from \(190.96\) to \(313.20\) infectious individuals and more than doubles cumulative infections from \(1086.42\) to \(2345.35\). Relative to baseline coupling, 50\% and 80\% restrictions reduce the epidemic peak by \(26.69\%\) and \(34.37\%\), and cumulative infections by \(25.07\%\) and \(41.48\%\), respectively. Conversely, a 50\% increase in spatial coupling raises the peak by \(30.14\%\) and cumulative infections by \(23.54\%\). Although local transmission remains dominant in every division, cross-patch infection accounts for \(28.83\%\) of new infections in Rajshahi at the baseline epidemic peak. Source-sink analysis identifies Dhaka as the dominant cross-patch source and Chattogram as a smaller secondary source.
tldr: A multipatch epidemiological model analyzes interdivisional connectivity and vaccination dynamics for the 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak, estimating local reproduction numbers and evaluating spatial coupling effects.
motivation: The 2026 measles resurgence in Bangladesh motivates a spatial modeling framework that accounts for heterogeneous local transmission, vaccination activity, and interdivisional connectivity.
method: The authors formulate a multipatch susceptible-vaccinated-infectious-recovered model for eight administrative divisions, estimate division-specific parameters using bounded nonlinear least squares with 1000 parametric bootstrap replicates, and connect divisions via compartment-specific movement and cross-patch infection coefficients.
result: Estimated local reproduction numbers range from 1.1386 in Khulna to 4.3491 in Dhaka, with Chattogram also high; baseline spatial coupling increases the network-wide peak from 190.96 to 313.20 infectious individuals and more than doubles cumulative infections from 1086.42 to 2345.35.
conclusion: Local transmission remains dominant in every division, but cross-patch infection contributes significantly (e.g., 28.83% in Rajshahi at peak), with Dhaka as the dominant source, highlighting the importance of spatial restrictions and vaccination for outbreak control.

title: Certifying Non-existence Of Integer Points On Curves
authors: Eugene Go Bogdan Grechuk
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18916v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an elementary but powerful method for proving that a two-variable equation has no integer solutions. The method produces quadratic identities which every integer solution must satisfy. Once these identities are established, a standard quadratic reciprocity argument finishes the proof. We illustrate the power of the method by resolving [MATH] out of [MATH] two-variable equations of size up to [MATH] for which the problem of integer solubility remained open. We also resolve the remaining [MATH] equations by deeper methods, and further determine the integer solubility of all two-variable equations of size up to [MATH] and of length up to [MATH], with two exceptions. Before this work, there were [MATH] equations in this category that resisted the previously known methods, and we proved that [MATH] of them have no integer solutions, with all proofs formalized in Lean. In addition, we show that our method can be used to solve certain two-variable equations whose integer solution set is non-empty.
tldr: The paper presents an elementary method using quadratic identities and quadratic reciprocity to prove that certain two-variable Diophantine equations have no integer solutions, resolving many previously open cases with Lean-formalized proofs.
motivation: Determining integer solubility of two-variable equations is a longstanding problem in number theory, and many small-size equations remained unresolved by known methods.
method: The authors derive quadratic identities that any integer solution must satisfy, then complete the proof via a standard quadratic reciprocity argument, formalizing results in Lean.
result: They resolve a large batch of previously open two-variable equations, proving many have no integer solutions, and also handle equations with non-empty solution sets.
conclusion: The approach is elementary yet powerful, substantially extending the known classification of integer solubility for small two-variable equations, with machine-checked proofs.

title: Packing Intermediate Dimensions Of Measures And Applications
authors: Nicolas Angelini
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a spectrum of dimensions of measures, the [MATH], [MATH], of a Borel probability measure [MATH] on [MATH] and the [MATH]. We show that this spectrum encodes the information on [MATH] that governs the packing dimension of its projections and H\"{o}lder images. First, [MATH] is the exact threshold for the packing dimension profiles of Falconer and Howroyd: for every real [MATH] and [MATH] for which our bound gives the exact value [MATH] for almost every [MATH]-dimensional subspace [MATH], whereas the bound of Falconer and Mattila is strictly smaller. As applications, for a large family of random [MATH]-H\"{o}lder maps [MATH], we prove that, for compactly supported [MATH], [MATH] almost surely if and only if [MATH], and that the packing analogue of Kahane's formula holds for fractional Brownian motions if and only if [MATH]. Analogous results are obtained for analytic sets.

motivation: The packing dimension of projections and images of measures under Hölder maps is governed by delicate dimensional thresholds, and existing bounds by Falconer and Mattila are not always sharp.
method: The author defines a spectrum of intermediate dimensions for measures and proves that it gives the exact threshold for packing dimension profiles, with applications to random Hölder maps and fractional Brownian motions.

conclusion: This spectrum of dimensions sharpens the geometric measure theory of projections and images, with analogues for analytic sets.

title: From A Student's Question To The Half-Derivative: A Constructivist Teaching Model - Part I
authors: Davit Kapanadze
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a conceptual, cognitive-constructivist model for teaching the half-derivative. The model starts from a student's question and frames it as the problem of generalizing the familiar operation of differentiation. On a suitably chosen space of monomials, under the assumptions of linearity and of lowering the exponent by one half, the requirement that the operator applied twice give the ordinary derivative produces a recurrence for the coefficients. The freedom of normalization becomes visible, and an additional convention yields a formula compatible with the monomial rule of the Riemann-Liouville half-derivative. The domain of the operator and its relation to the Riemann-Liouville and Caputo operators are treated separately. The mathematical results rest on the author's earlier preprints; the contribution of this paper is their transformation into an instructional pathway organized in phases, with diagnostic questions, an analysis of typical errors, and comparative problems. The model is a design proposal: its effectiveness has not yet been established by systematic empirical research. The interactive Socratic implementation and the detailed diagnostics are the subject of Part II.
tldr: The paper presents a conceptual, cognitive-constructivist teaching model that introduces the half-derivative starting from a student's question about generalizing differentiation.
motivation: The work aims to transform mathematical results on the half-derivative into an instructional pathway for teaching fractional calculus.
method: On a space of monomials, assuming linearity and a half-exponent reduction, the author derives a recurrence for coefficients and explores normalization conventions to connect with the Riemann-Liouville half-derivative.
result: A formula compatible with the monomial rule of the Riemann-Liouville half-derivative is obtained, along with a phased instructional design including diagnostic questions and typical errors.
conclusion: The model is a design proposal whose effectiveness has not yet been empirically established; the Socratic implementation and detailed diagnostics are left for Part II.

title: Generalized Pellet's Theorem For Analytic Matrix-valued Functions
authors: Hiromochi Itoh, Kei Matsushima, Takayuki Yamada
abstract: ArXiv:2610.18941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generalized Pellet's theorem is extended to analytic matrix-valued functions using Descartes' rule of signs for infinite series. Cauchy's estimate is incorporated to allow numerical computation of the bounds. To address the issue that Pellet's theorem and its generalizations may not always guarantee the existence of bounds, for the case of matrix size one, we employ the Dandelin- Lobachevsky-Graeffe method, which ensures the existence of the bounds for the roots and further improves them as the order of the transform increases. Without the need for any a priori information on the function, these theorems allow us to compute mathematically verified bounds for the roots in a certain region using an interval arithmetic implementation of the function. Numerical examples and an implementation are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
tldr: The paper generalizes Pellet's theorem to analytic matrix-valued functions, using Descartes' rule of signs, Cauchy's estimate, and interval arithmetic to compute verified root bounds.
motivation: Classical Pellet-type theorems provide root bounds for scalar analytic functions, but extensions to matrix-valued functions and guaranteed existence of bounds remain limited.
method: The authors extend Pellet's theorem via Descartes' rule for infinite series, incorporate Cauchy's estimate for numerical bounding, and use the Dandelin-Lobachevsky-Graeffe method in the scalar case to guarantee and improve bounds.
result: The proposed approach yields mathematically verified bounds for roots in a region without a priori information, supported by interval-arithmetic implementation and numerical examples.
conclusion: The generalized theorems and implementation provide an effective framework for certified root localization of analytic matrix-valued functions, though the work is purely mathematical and outside the specified quantum research directions.

title: Exponential Stability Of Slow--Fast Stochastic Systems With A Small Delay
authors: Yudong Wang, Kele Sun, Shijie Zhou, Xuerong Mao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the exponential stability of coupled slow--fast stochastic systems with a small delay. Under an averaged Lyapunov condition, we establish practical [MATH]th-moment exponential stability for [MATH] using a cutoff-function approach to handle singular Lyapunov derivatives near the origin. Exponential stability in the [MATH]th moment and almost surely is further obtained through two distinct mechanisms: homogeneous dissipation of the fast dynamics or vanishing sensitivity of the slow coefficients to the fast state near the origin. We extend these results to locally Lipschitz systems, establishing exponential stability with arbitrarily high probability for bounded sets of initial data, thereby broadening the applicability of stability analysis for stochastic systems with delayed feedback. Numerical examples illustrate our results.
tldr: The paper studies exponential stability of coupled slow-fast stochastic systems with a small delay using an averaged Lyapunov condition and cutoff-function approach.
motivation: Slow-fast stochastic systems with delays arise in applications requiring stability guarantees, but singular Lyapunov derivatives near the origin complicate analysis.
method: The authors use an averaged Lyapunov condition and a cutoff-function approach to handle singularities, establishing practical moment exponential stability and extending results to locally Lipschitz systems.
result: They derive th-moment and almost sure exponential stability via homogeneous dissipation of the fast dynamics or vanishing sensitivity of slow coefficients near the origin, with high-probability guarantees for bounded initial data.
conclusion: The work broadens stability analysis for delayed stochastic systems and is illustrated with numerical examples, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Sharp Discrete Sobolev Inequality And Left Inverses Of Higher Order Differences
authors: Raul Hindov, Shahaf Nitzan, Jan-Fredrik Olsen, Eskil Rydhe
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For integers [MATH], we determine the best constants in the inequalities [MATH] where [MATH] is the difference operator. We find that these constants correspond to the [MATH] norm of the discrete Chebyshev polynomials, and show that the extremal sequences may be obtained by appropriate sampling of the discrete Landau polynomials. From beginning to end, this project was carried out without use of AI.
tldr: The paper determines sharp constants in discrete Sobolev inequalities for higher-order difference operators and characterizes extremal sequences via discrete Chebyshev and Landau polynomials.
motivation: The authors aim to establish best constants for discrete Sobolev-type inequalities involving finite difference operators, a problem in classical approximation theory and discrete harmonic analysis.
method: They analyze left inverses of higher-order difference operators and connect the sharp constants to the norms of discrete Chebyshev polynomials, using sampling of discrete Landau polynomials to obtain extremal sequences.
result: The optimal constants are identified explicitly as the norms of discrete Chebyshev polynomials, and extremal sequences are constructed by appropriate sampling of discrete Landau polynomials.
conclusion: The work provides a complete solution to the sharp-constant problem for these discrete inequalities and links it to classical orthogonal polynomials, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Mixing Rates For Analytic Observables: Toral Endomorphisms And Anosov Blaschke Deformations
authors: Ekaterina Shchetka
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze exponential mixing for analytic observables and show that mixing at a double exponential rate occurs for genuinely nonlinear systems. Neither its presence nor its sharp exponent is stable under arbitrarily small area-preserving perturbations in the real-analytic topology. We construct two families of area-preserving Anosov Blaschke product diffeomorphisms that converge in the real-analytic topology to the same hyperbolic toral automorphism. For nonzero parameters, both deformations are topologically conjugate to the linear model but not [MATH]-conjugate. For all nonzero parameter values, the maps in the first family are mixing at a double exponential rate with the same sharp exponent, strictly smaller than that of the linear map. The sharp exponent is therefore not lower semicontinuous at the linear map. In the second family, mixing at a double exponential rate is lost altogether, although the maps remain exponentially mixing. We also establish double exponential bounds for every ergodic toral endomorphism and uniform bounds of the same type for totally ergodic higher-rank toral actions. Our method combines the Fourier escape argument with Koopman operator estimates from a Hilbert space of analytic functions to its dual space of hyperfunctions.
tldr: The paper studies exponential mixing rates for analytic observables in nonlinear dynamical systems, including toral endomorphisms and Anosov Blaschke deformations, showing instability of double-exponential mixing under real-analytic perturbations.
motivation: The author aims to understand whether and how sharp mixing rates for analytic observables are stable under small perturbations in smooth dynamical systems.
method: The approach combines a Fourier escape argument with Koopman operator estimates between a Hilbert space of analytic functions and its dual space of hyperfunctions.
result: Two families of area-preserving Anosov Blaschke product diffeomorphisms are constructed that converge to the same hyperbolic toral automorphism; one family mixes at a strictly smaller double-exponential rate while the other loses double-exponential mixing but remains exponentially mixing.
conclusion: The sharp exponent for double-exponential mixing is not lower semicontinuous at the linear map, and double-exponential bounds are also established for ergodic toral endomorphisms and higher-rank toral actions.

title: Even And Odd Integer Values Of The Secondary Zeta Function
authors: Artur Kawalec
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The secondary zeta function is defined by $[MATH][MATH]\tfrac12+i\gamma[MATH]Z(s)[MATH]\xi[MATH][MATH][MATH]k\geq1[MATH][MATH][MATH][MATH][MATH]Z(k)[MATH]2\leq k\leq 7[MATH]L(x)[MATH]\xi(x+\tfrac12)[MATH]\gamma_1$, the ordinate of the first nontrivial zero, and demonstrate its convergence numerically.
tldr: The paper studies even and odd integer values of a secondary zeta function built from the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function and tests its numerical convergence.
motivation: The work explores special values and convergence properties of a zeta-like function defined via the ordinates of Riemann zeta zeros, aiming to understand its arithmetic behavior.
method: The secondary zeta function is defined using terms involving 1/2 + i gamma and related functions, with integer values computed for k between 2 and 7 and numerical convergence checked via L(x) and xi(x+1/2).
result: The paper reports explicit even and odd integer values of the secondary zeta function and demonstrates convergence numerically using the first nontrivial zero ordinate gamma_1.
conclusion: The results are purely number-theoretic and do not connect to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Aggregated Column Generation For Two-Stage Stochastic Mixed-Integer Programs
authors: Harshit Kothari, James Luedtke, Luke Marshall
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation applied to two-stage stochastic mixed-integer programs (SMIP) has been shown empirically to yield a formulation with strong bounds that can be solved via column generation. However, the time to solve the restricted master problem grows significantly with the number of scenarios due to the increasing number of nonanticipativity constraints (NACs). Moreover, the associated high-dimensional dual space can cause the dual multipliers to oscillate between iterations, further slowing convergence. We propose an aggregated column generation framework for solving a Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation. Applied to SMIP, this method partitions the NACs into groups and replaces each group with a weighted surrogate constraint, leading to a reduced size and providing implicit stabilization by restricting the dual space. While aggregation leads to a relaxation, we develop two strategies for recovering the standard Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation bound. The first iteratively refines the partition by splitting groups that contain violated constraints. The second keeps the partition fixed and adaptively updates the aggregation weights. We prove convergence of the two approaches and study their computational performance on two benchmark problem classes.
tldr: The paper proposes an aggregated column generation framework for solving two-stage stochastic mixed-integer programs, with convergence proofs and computational benchmarks.
motivation: Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation for two-stage SMIP yields strong bounds but suffers from many nonanticipativity constraints and dual oscillation as the number of scenarios grows.
method: It partitions nonanticipativity constraints into groups and replaces each group with a weighted surrogate constraint, then recovers the standard Dantzig-Wolfe bound via iterative partition refinement or adaptive weight updates.
result: Convergence of both recovery strategies is proven, and computational performance is studied on two benchmark problem classes.
conclusion: Aggregation reduces the master problem size and stabilizes duals while eventually matching the standard Dantzig-Wolfe bound.

title: Finite-sample Certification Of Coverage Regret For Budgeted Document Selection Under Adaptive Stratified Auditing
authors: Nora Serdyukova
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19207v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Selecting a budget-constrained set of documentary fragments, for instance the knowledge base of a retrieval-augmented generation system, raises a statistical question: how much expected query coverage is lost relative to the best feasible selection when the query distribution is unknown? We construct finite-sample, distribution-free upper confidence bounds for this coverage regret that remain valid after data-dependent selection. A pilot stage may select the document set, screen competitors, build comparison networks and learn an annotation policy. Then an independent audit acquires relevance labels with probabilities that are constant within observable strata. The main result is a simultaneous bound for all retained coverage contrasts. The bound is made observable by empirical-Bernstein variance calibration or by a one-stage construction without calibration, and it accounts for estimated stratum proportions. For maximum-type coverage we prove variance contractions for swaps of redundant fragments, give a condition under which multiscale radii improve on a direct union bound, and show that such redundancy cannot be certified from samples alone. A simulation study confirms validity and quantifies the gains from variance calibration and certified redundancy.
tldr: The paper derives finite-sample, distribution-free upper confidence bounds on coverage regret for budget-constrained document selection under adaptive stratified auditing.
motivation: Retrieval-augmented generation systems must pick a budget-limited set of knowledge-base fragments, and the expected query coverage lost relative to the best feasible selection is unknown when the query distribution is unknown and selection is data-dependent.
method: A pilot stage performs data-dependent selection, competitor screening, comparison-network construction, and annotation-policy learning, followed by an independent stratified audit; simultaneous confidence bounds are constructed via empirical-Bernstein variance calibration or a one-stage calibration-free construction accounting for estimated stratum proportions.
result: The authors prove a simultaneous bound valid for all retained coverage contrasts, establish variance contractions for swaps of redundant fragments, give a condition under which multiscale radii beat a direct union bound, and show redundancy cannot be certified from samples alone; simulations confirm validity and quantify gains.
conclusion: The framework provides rigorous distribution-free certification of coverage regret in adaptive document selection, though certified redundancy reductions require structural assumptions beyond sampled data.

title: Solving A Sequence Of Eigenvalue Problems Using Snapshot And Row Subsampling
authors: Yuji Nakatsukasa Francesco Hrobat
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A sequence of eigenvalue problems requires solving [MATH] where [MATH], [MATH] and (usually) [MATH] is the largest or smallest eigenvalue of [MATH]. Often, the matrices [MATH] come from a discretization of a smooth map depending on a parameter [MATH], that is [MATH], so the matrices [MATH] change gradually along the sequence. Under this latter assumption, we introduce an efficient algorithm for solving sequences of eigenvalue problems. Our algorithm combines the ideas of reduced order model and row subsampling, as done in [E. Jones and Y. Nakatsukasa, arXiv, 2025] for linear systems. In addition, in our approach, the same set of rows is guaranteed to work well independently of the value of the parameter [MATH] or the matrix [MATH] as long as the snapshot matrix is unchanged and given that the row subset was chosen well at the beginning. Furthermore, we implement an update strategy of the snapshot matrix. Along these results, we present theoretical analysis of the snapshot matrix for eigenvalue problems, showing an exponential decay of the singular values, and we give bounds on the error on eigenvectors for unseen value of the parameter. This analysis generalizes that in [M. Guido, D. Kressner, and P. Ricci, J. Sci. Comput., 2024] and shows that, regardless of the distribution of the snapshot points, the convergence is always (asymptotically) exponential in the number of snapshot points if the function [MATH] admits an analytical extension. We further generalize our algorithm for computing largest or smallest singular values and relative singular vectors and to generalized eigenvalue problems. We conclude with numerical results showing the efficiency of our approach.
tldr: Introduces an efficient algorithm for solving sequences of parameter-dependent eigenvalue problems by combining reduced order modeling with row subsampling, supported by theoretical error bounds.
motivation: Solving many related eigenvalue problems arising from discretized parameter-dependent smooth maps can be computationally expensive, and existing methods often do not exploit the gradual change of matrices along the sequence.
method: The algorithm combines snapshot-based reduced order modeling with row subsampling, where a single well-chosen row subset remains effective across parameter values, and includes an update strategy for the snapshot matrix.
result: Theoretical analysis shows exponential decay of singular values of the snapshot matrix and bounds on eigenvector error for unseen parameters, generalizing prior work by proving asymptotic exponential convergence under analytic extension regardless of snapshot distribution.
conclusion: The approach efficiently handles sequences of eigenvalue problems, largest/smallest singular values, and generalized eigenvalue problems, with numerical results confirming its effectiveness, though it lies outside quantum information research.

title: Discrete Edge Multiscale Space Based Hybrid Schwarz Preconditioner For High-Frequency Helmholtz Problems
authors: Shubin Fu, Shihua Gong, Guanglian Li, Yueqi Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop a novel hybrid Schwarz method, termed as edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz (EMs-HS), for solving the Helmholtz problem with large wavenumbers. The problem is discretized using [MATH]-conforming nodal finite element methods on meshes of size [MATH] decreasing faster than [MATH] such that the discretization error can be bounded by the data uniformly with respect to [MATH]. EMs-HS consists of a one-level Schwarz preconditioner (RAS-imp) and a coarse solver in a multiplicative way. The RAS-imp preconditioner solves local problems on overlapping subdomains with impedance boundary conditions in parallel, and combines the local solutions using partition of unity. On the PDE level, this coarse space corresponds to an edge multiscale space proposed in {[S. Fu, G. Li, R. Craster, and S. Guenneau, , 19(4):1684-1709, 2021]}. The approximation properties of this coarse space to the discrete solutions from the primal and adjoint problems are derived by a novel conforming Galerkin finite element method based upon a nonstandard variational formulation. This work represents the first theoretical analysis of an edge multiscale space at the discrete level. We prove that the EMs-HS preconditioner leads to a convergent fixed-point iteration uniformly for large wavenumbers, by rigorously analyzing the approximation properties of the coarse space to the global Helmholtz harmonic extension part and to the solution of the adjoint problem. We provide extensive numerical results on the sharpness of the theoretical findings and also demonstrate the method on challenging heterogeneous models.
tldr: The paper develops an edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz (EMs-HS) preconditioner for solving high-frequency Helmholtz problems with large wavenumbers.
motivation: High-wavenumber Helmholtz problems are notoriously difficult to solve numerically because standard preconditioners degrade as the wavenumber increases. The authors aim for a wavenumber-robust iterative solver with rigorous theoretical guarantees.
method: A one-level RAS-imp Schwarz preconditioner with impedance boundary conditions on overlapping subdomains is combined multiplicatively with a coarse solver corresponding to an edge multiscale space, analyzed via a novel conforming Galerkin finite element formulation on a nonstandard variational form.
result: The authors prove the EMs-HS preconditioner yields a convergent fixed-point iteration uniformly in the wavenumber, supported by extensive numerical experiments including challenging heterogeneous models.
conclusion: The work provides the first discrete-level theoretical analysis of an edge multiscale space and demonstrates a scalable preconditioner for high-frequency Helmholtz problems.

title: A Stabilized Cr-cr Method For Fourth-Order Elliptic Problems
authors: Yule Sun, Shudan Tian, Qian Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a CR-CR method for strain gradient elasticity and prove its robustness with respect to the Lame parameter [MATH] and the length scale [MATH]. The method introduces the strain as an independent symmetric tensor and discretizes both the strain and the displacement using CR elements. The commuting properties of the CR interpolation operator with the relevant differential operators leads the robustness with respect to [MATH]. A stabilization term weakly imposes the relation between the strain and the symmetric gradient of the displacement. The method also applies directly to the biharmonic equation and singularly perturbed fourth-order problems. For these problems, we prove that the CR-CR method is equivalent to an RT-CR method proposed by Huang and Tang. This result extends the classical equivalence between the RT-P0 mixed method and the CR method for the Poisson equation to fourth-order problems. The equivalence shows that the stabilization term arises naturally from the RT-CR mixed formulation.
tldr: The paper proposes a stabilized CR-CR finite element method for fourth-order elliptic problems and proves its robustness and equivalence to an RT-CR mixed method.
motivation: Fourth-order elliptic problems, such as strain gradient elasticity and the biharmonic equation, require stable and robust numerical discretizations, especially with respect to material parameters and length scales.
method: The method uses CR elements for both strain and displacement, introduces a stabilization term to weakly impose the strain-displacement relation, and exploits commuting properties of the CR interpolation operator.
result: The CR-CR method is proved robust with respect to the Lamé parameter and length scale, and is shown to be equivalent to the RT-CR method for biharmonic and singularly perturbed fourth-order problems.
conclusion: The equivalence naturally explains the stabilization term as arising from the RT-CR mixed formulation, extending a classical equivalence from second-order to fourth-order problems.

title: Maximin Share Allocations For Two Types Of Items
authors: Yu Chen, Kai Jie Wong, Xiaorui Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the fair allocation of indivisible items among [MATH] agents with additive valuations (or costs) using the fairness notion of maximin share (MMS). Since MMS allocations do not always exist when [MATH], one direction in the literature has been to identify special classes of instances in which exact MMS allocations can be guaranteed. We show that, when items can be divided into two types of chores, MMS allocations always exist and can be computed in polynomial time using a novel geometric approach inspired by prior work in job scheduling. We further discuss how our technique extends to instances with two types of goods, as well as mixed instances consisting of one type of objective good and one type of objective chore.
tldr: The paper proves that maximin share (MMS) allocations always exist for instances with two types of chores and can be computed in polynomial time via a geometric approach.
motivation: MMS allocations do not always exist for general additive valuations, so identifying special classes of instances where exact MMS allocations are guaranteed is an important line of work.
method: The authors develop a novel geometric approach inspired by job scheduling to construct MMS allocations for two types of chores, and extend the technique to two types of goods and mixed good/chore instances.
result: For two types of chores, MMS allocations always exist and can be found in polynomial time; the method also handles two types of goods and mixed cases.
conclusion: This work expands the set of known instances with guaranteed MMS allocations and provides efficient algorithms for such structured fair division problems.

title: Beyond Maliciousness: Static And Runtime Attack-Surface Profiling Of Agent Skills
authors: Ratnesh Pandey, Japneet Singh, Harsh Akshit, Sonali Tyagi, Cassie Crossley
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills are Markdown documents that a tool-using agent reads as instructions and then acts on with the privileges of the session that loaded them. Installing one grants authority (the standing to direct the agent, not new privilege), and the size of that grant is what we measure. We present a two-phase attack-surface profiling methodology that combines whole-bundle static analysis and dependency provenance checking with instrumented sandbox execution and separate model-based assessment of the resulting traces. We apply the methodology to 6,309 listings from two marketplaces, selecting listings for execution without conditioning that decision on a prior threat or risk signal. Half the corpus carries evidence of shell-execution capability; the corresponding shares are 35% for filesystem read, 31% each for filesystem write and network egress, and 13% for credential access; seven listings in ten carry at least one elevated capability. That is the surface a user accepts at install time, and almost none of it is visible then. A permission model exists but is close to inert. Authors may list the tools a skill pre-approves in its own frontmatter, which removes confirmation prompts rather than restricting what the skill can reach; of the 6,061 listings whose frontmatter parses, 770 declare anything at all, the vocabulary cannot express credential or environment access, and nothing checks what it does express against the bundle. Declaring is also not declaring accurately: 59% of declaring listings understate what their bundle can do. ClawHub declares roughly twice as often as skillsmp, yet under-declares on 88% of its declarations against 31%. Triage at the marketplace boundary therefore cannot rest on what a listing declares. It must rest on what the bundle can do. These results position capability-oriented attack-surface profiling as a necessary complement to maliciousness detection.
tldr: The paper presents a two-phase methodology for profiling the attack surface of agent skills, combining static bundle analysis with instrumented sandbox execution, and finds widespread elevated capabilities and under-declaration across two marketplaces.
motivation: Agent skills are Markdown instructions that grant authority to tool-using agents, but their true capability surface is largely invisible at install time, motivating better profiling before deployment.
method: The authors combine whole-bundle static analysis and dependency provenance checking with instrumented sandbox execution, followed by separate model-based assessment of execution traces, applied to 6,309 marketplace listings selected without prior threat conditioning.
result: Half the corpus shows shell-execution capability, 70% carry at least one elevated capability, and 59% of declaring listings understate what their bundle can do; the existing permission model is close to inert and cannot express credential or environment access.
conclusion: Marketplace triage cannot rely on declarations and should instead use capability-oriented attack-surface profiling as a necessary complement to maliciousness detection.

title: Truthful And Expected-Payment-Optimal Model Routing In Graph-Based Agentic Workflows
authors: Jiayuan Liu, Mingyu Guo, Jiarui Gan, Vincent Conitzer
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assigning routine tasks to cheaper large language model (LLM) providers can reduce generation cost, but switching providers may require processing accumulated context again. Keeping dependent tasks with the same provider can instead reuse eligible context. Graph-based workflows therefore couple routing decisions across tasks. Independent providers may also privately know their real-time unit costs and strategically misreport them. We formulate this routing problem as a single-parameter procurement auction and propose STAR (Strategy-proof Topology-aware Agent Routing), which minimizes virtual-cost-weighted graph workloads. Its allocation rule and payments, computed by integrating workload over possible cost reports, make truthful reporting utility-maximizing regardless of other providers' reports and cover each truthful provider's execution cost. With independent cost distributions and non-decreasing virtual costs, STAR additionally minimizes the user's expected total payment to providers. Controlled synthetic experiments separate the execution-cost benefit of topology awareness from the payment benefit of virtual-cost optimization: the former grows with fan-out and transferred payload, while the latter increases gradually along the tested prior-shape heterogeneity path. A paired sensitivity study quantifies how payment savings vary with prior misspecification while strategy-proofness is preserved.
tldr: The paper formulates routing tasks among LLM providers in graph-based agentic workflows as a single-parameter procurement auction and proposes STAR, a strategy-proof, expected-payment-optimal routing mechanism.
motivation: Assigning routine tasks to cheaper LLM providers can reduce cost, but context reuse and strategic cost misreporting by providers complicate routing in dependent graph-based workflows.
method: The authors model the problem as a procurement auction, define a topology-aware virtual-cost-weighted workload minimization, and design STAR to compute allocations and payments via integrating workload over cost reports.
result: STAR ensures truthful reporting is utility-maximizing and covers truthful providers' execution costs; under independent cost distributions and non-decreasing virtual costs, it also minimizes expected total payment, with experiments separating topology and payment benefits.
conclusion: Topology-aware routing and virtual-cost optimization yield distinct benefits, and STAR preserves strategy-proofness even under prior misspecification, making it a practical mechanism for LLM provider routing.

title: Aware-rg: Abstraction Aware Explanation Of Resiliency Graphs For Cyber Physical Systems
authors: Shadaab Kawnain Bashir, Rakesh Podder, Philip D. Hopkins, Sarath Sreedharan, Indrakshi Ray, Indrajit Ray
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the security posture of cyber physical systems (CPS) requires reasoning across both information technology (IT) and operational technology (OT). However, a security analyst often holds an incomplete, role-specific view of the underlying system which has most likely resulted from their knowledge limited by a need-to-know framework. Such an incomplete view can potentially lead them to incorrectly assess if a cyber attack produces an untoward physical consequence resulting in making uninformed decisions about system resilience. In this work, we present AWARE-RG (Abstraction Aware Explanation of Resiliency Graphs), a semi-automated, human-in-the-loop framework that provides an analyst with a role-bounded, need-to-know explanations of resiliency paths in a CPS. The AWARE-RG abstraction structure is derived using Formal Concept Analysis over MITRE ATT&CK for ICS tactics, ordered by the ICS Cyber Kill Chain. For valid attack-fault queries, plan repair and backward means-end analysis identify the missing dependencies, explain why the physical hazard is reachable, and suggest defensive strategies. For invalid attack-fault queries, AWARE-RG localizes the first abstraction level at which the path fails, and reports confirmed blocking conditions as hardening pointers.
tldr: AWARE-RG is a semi-automated framework for explaining role-bounded resiliency paths in cyber-physical systems by abstracting MITRE ATT&CK for ICS tactics and using plan repair/backward means-end analysis.
motivation: Security analysts often have incomplete, role-specific views of CPS due to need-to-know constraints, which can lead to incorrect assessment of cyber-physical attack consequences and resilience decisions.
method: The framework derives an abstraction structure via Formal Concept Analysis over MITRE ATT&CK for ICS tactics ordered by the ICS Cyber Kill Chain, then uses plan repair and backward means-end analysis to explain valid attack-fault queries, and localizes failure levels for invalid queries.
result: AWARE-RG provides role-bounded explanations for valid attack-fault queries by identifying missing dependencies and suggesting defenses, while for invalid queries it reports the first failing abstraction level and confirmed blocking conditions as hardening pointers.
conclusion: AWARE-RG offers a human-in-the-loop approach to improve CPS security posture understanding through abstraction-aware explanations, though it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Analyzing And Mitigating Poisoning Attacks On Flow-Based Intrusion Detection
authors: Florian Spelter, Johannes F. Loevenich, Tobias H\"urten, Erik Adler, Maxime Schwarzer, Laurin Holz, Roberto Rigolin F. Lopes
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) are increasingly deployed in operational networks, their dependence on large-scale training data introduces a critical vulnerability to stealthy poisoning attacks. We demonstrate that latent backdoors can be successfully implanted in flow-based IDS models by poisoning as little as 0.001% of the training data, maintaining near-nominal performance on clean inputs while ensuring high attack success rates. To address this threat, we propose a diagnostic-first methodology that localizes trigger-relevant features through constrained perturbation analysis and detects poisoning-induced behavioral drift by comparison with a distilled baseline model. The proposed methodology further enables targeted mitigation via automated data sanitization or neuron pruning. Our findings expose the operational risks of near-undetectable backdoors and provide a scalable approach to analyzing, quantifying, and mitigating backdoor exposure in AI-based IDS.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that latent backdoors can be implanted in flow-based intrusion detection models by poisoning as little as 0.001% of training data, and proposes a diagnostic-first methodology to detect and mitigate such poisoning attacks.
motivation: AI-based intrusion detection systems rely on large-scale training data, which introduces a critical vulnerability to stealthy poisoning attacks that can implant near-undetectable backdoors.
method: The authors poison a tiny fraction of training data to implant latent backdoors, then localize trigger-relevant features via constrained perturbation analysis and detect poisoning-induced behavioral drift by comparison with a distilled baseline model; mitigation is achieved through automated data sanitization or neuron pruning.
result: Latent backdoors are successfully implanted while maintaining near-nominal performance on clean inputs and achieving high attack success rates, and the proposed diagnostic-first method localizes triggers and enables targeted mitigation.
conclusion: The findings expose the operational risks of near-undetectable backdoors in AI-based IDS and provide a scalable approach for analyzing, quantifying, and mitigating backdoor exposure.

title: Adaptive And Proximal Federated Optimization For Transferable Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Rezwan Islam Salvi, MD Rafin Jawad Hafiz, Abeer Mahmood Kalam, Md Moniruzzaman
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) based on deep learning often fail to detect attack classes that are absent from training data, limiting their robustness against zero-day threats. This property called transferability across attack classes, remains underexplored especially in federated learning (FL) settings where data heterogeneity and client drift pose additional challenges. Prior work (TabFIDS) showed that FedAvg combined with bootstrapping and temporal averaging improves transferability for cross-device NIDS. In this paper, we explore whether other federated optimizers can do better. We compare two optimizers inspired by FedAdam and FedProx against the FedAvg baseline on the CIC-IDS 2017 dataset using an 11-client federated setup, sweep 10 hyperparameter configurations, and contrast two data-balancing strategies: bootstrapping and SMOTE. Using the count of client pairs whose transferred-model accuracy exceeds 70% as our primary metric (following TabFIDS), the proximal optimizer with a strong regularization term yields 48 transferable pairs versus 42 for FedAvg, while the adaptive optimizer with an aggressive server learning rate yields 46 pairs. SMOTE improves per-pair accuracy over bootstrapping but reduces breadth, revealing a depth-vs-breadth trade-off: high accuracy on a few client pairs versus moderate accuracy across most. These results indicate that the choice of federated optimizer, the rule by which client updates are regularized and aggregated into the global model, is very important for federated NIDS.
tldr: This paper compares federated optimization algorithms (FedProx, FedAdam-like) for network intrusion detection, finding that proximal regularization improves transferability across attack classes.
motivation: Deep learning NIDS often fail on unseen attack classes, and transferability in federated learning settings with heterogeneous data is underexplored.
method: They benchmark two federated optimizers inspired by FedAdam and FedProx against FedAvg on CIC-IDS 2017 with 11 clients, sweeping 10 hyperparameter configurations and comparing bootstrapping versus SMOTE balancing.
result: The proximal optimizer with strong regularization yields 48 transferable client pairs vs. 42 for FedAvg, while the adaptive optimizer yields 46; SMOTE improves per-pair accuracy but reduces breadth.
conclusion: The choice of federated optimizer and regularization/aggregation rule significantly impacts transferability, revealing a depth-vs-breadth trade-off in federated NIDS.

title: Finite Satisfiability Of Two-Variable Logic With Arbitrarily Many Successors
authors: Artur Je\.z, Jakub Michaliszyn, Piotr Witkowski
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite satisfiability of two-variable first-order logic over structures equipped with an arbitrary finite number of independent successor relations of linear orders. The number of successor relations is part of the input, and the vocabulary may contain further unrestricted unary and binary relations. We prove decidability in deterministic doubly exponential space together with a triply exponential bound on the size of a smallest finite model. This settles the unrestricted finite case beyond two successors.
tldr: The paper studies the decidability and complexity of finite satisfiability for two-variable first-order logic extended with arbitrarily many independent successor relations of linear orders.
motivation: Finite satisfiability of two-variable logic with a fixed number of successor relations is known, but the unrestricted finite case beyond two successors has remained open.
method: The authors establish decidability via a deterministic doubly exponential space algorithm and prove a triply exponential upper bound on the size of the smallest finite model.
result: The unrestricted finite satisfiability problem for two-variable logic with arbitrarily many successor relations is decidable in deterministic doubly exponential space, with a triply exponential small-model bound.
conclusion: This settles the unrestricted finite case beyond two successors and advances the understanding of the complexity landscape of two-variable logic with order successors.

title: No-Regret Learning In Stackelberg Security Games With An Unknown, Bounded Set Of Attacker Types
authors: Sabil Ahmad, Ishita, Aditi Singh, Swaprava Nath
abstract: ArXiv:2610.20066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a repeated Stackelberg security game, a defender commits in every round to a randomized allocation of its resources, and an attacker, drawn from a set of types, best-responds. Existing no-regret guarantees assume that the defender knows this set of types in advance. We drop this assumption: the set of types is unknown, and its size is at most [MATH], an upper bound that the defender is not told. We show that what can be learned then depends on what the defender observes. If it observes the type of each attacker, an algorithm that adds types to its list as they appear achieves regret [MATH] over [MATH] rounds with [MATH] targets, the same [MATH] rate as with known types, at an extra factor of only [MATH] and without ever using [MATH]. If it observes only the attacked target and types come from an infinite universe, no algorithm has sublinear regret: in a fixed three-target game every algorithm suffers regret at least [MATH], even against a single attacker type, because it cannot tell which type it faces. If, in addition, it is told every [MATH] rounds which types have appeared so far, sublinear regret returns, at [MATH]. The first term is the rate of the partial-information learner we use, and we show that the additive cost of the delay cannot be avoided.
tldr: The paper studies no-regret learning in repeated Stackelberg security games when the defender does not know the set of attacker types, characterizing when sublinear regret is achievable under different observation models.
motivation: Existing no-regret guarantees in Stackelberg security games assume the defender knows the attacker type set in advance, which is often unrealistic.
method: The authors analyze regret under three information regimes: observing each attacker's type, observing only the attacked target, and receiving delayed type information, using partial-information learning algorithms.
result: With full type observation, regret scales as the known-type rate up to logarithmic factors; with only attacked-target observation, no sublinear regret is possible; with delayed type information, sublinear regret returns at a cost that cannot be avoided.
conclusion: Learning in unknown-type Stackelberg security games is possible only under sufficiently informative feedback, and fundamental limits arise when feedback is too weak.

title: A Deep Energy Method Formulation For Phase-field Modelling Of Ductile Fracture
authors: Nojus Plung\.e, Peter Brommer, Rachel S. Edwards, Emmanouil G. Kakouris
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work extends the Deep Energy Method to phase-field modelling of ductile fracture in elasto-plastic solids. Its key contribution is an incremental DEM-based formulation that couples history-dependent J2 plasticity and plasticity-dependent fracture toughness with separate energy-optimised displacement and phase-field representations. The formulation combines the second-order Ambrosio-Tortorelli phase-field fracture model with small-strain J2 plasticity and linear isotropic hardening. A volumetric-deviatoric split defines the elastic crack-driving energy, while accumulated equivalent plastic strain governs the degradation of local fracture toughness. Plastic internal variables are updated locally through radial return. The reduced energy is minimised alternately with respect to the displacement and phase fields, represented by a ReZero residual neural network and spatially localised Gaussian radial basis functions with trainable centres, respectively. This split addresses the diffuse phase-field profiles observed in preliminary calculations with a shared global network. Alternating optimisation is combined with transfer learning to reuse trainable parameters and optimiser states across loading increments, while the converged constitutive history is carried forward separately at quadrature points. The numerical results demonstrate close agreement with finite-element reference solutions in predicting force-displacement responses, energy evolution, plastic deformation and crack propagation. The framework captures the main features of ductile fracture, although accuracy becomes more sensitive to loading increments near abrupt fracture events.
tldr: This paper extends the Deep Energy Method to phase-field modelling of ductile fracture in elasto-plastic solids by coupling J2 plasticity with plasticity-dependent fracture toughness.
motivation: Phase-field fracture models for ductile materials are computationally expensive with conventional finite-element methods, motivating the use of energy-based neural network solvers.
method: An incremental DEM formulation combines the second-order Ambrosio-Tortorelli phase-field fracture model with small-strain J2 plasticity and linear isotropic hardening, using separate ReZero residual networks for displacement and Gaussian radial basis functions for the phase field, optimised alternately with transfer learning.
result: Numerical results show close agreement with finite-element reference solutions for force-displacement responses, energy evolution, plastic deformation, and crack propagation, though accuracy becomes sensitive to loading increments near abrupt fracture events.
conclusion: The framework successfully captures the main features of ductile fracture, but is a computational solid mechanics contribution with no connection to quantum information theory, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On The Mathematical Structure Of Helical Shear In Anelastic Continua
authors: Souhayl Sadik, Giuseppe Saccomandi, Luigi Vergori
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study helical shear of a thick-walled tube made of an incompressible, isotropic hyper-anelastic solid carrying a radially symmetric distribution of axial screw dislocations. Through the Bilby--Kr\"oner--Lee decomposition, the dislocations are encoded in a Weitzenb\"ock material manifold, whose Riemannian metric alone enters the elastic response. Equilibrium reduces at each radius to an algebraic system for the azimuthal and axial shear strains, whose cross terms are proportional to the dislocation strength and to the dependence of the strain energy on the second invariant; the two shear modes therefore couple only in the presence of dislocations. Exact solutions are obtained for neo-Hookean, Fung--Demiray, Gent, Knowles, and Mooney--Rivlin materials, and numerical ones for Gent--Gent materials. The universal relations of Horgan and Saccomandi are extended to dislocated generalized neo-Hookean tubes. Dislocations stiffen the tube when the strain energy stiffens with the first invariant, couple the two shear modes chirally when it depends on the second, and may restrict admissibility: they cap the dislocation strength in Gent and Gent--Gent materials, and contract the admissible traction region in Knowles materials with power-law index below n = 1/2. A weakly nonlinear analysis to third order in the applied tractions and dislocation strength shows that, at first order (linear elasticity), the dislocations leave the shear response unaffected while carrying a residual stress. The chiral coupling enters at second order, through the dependence of the strain energy on the second invariant, so that every dislocated material couples the modes as the Mooney--Rivlin solid with the same second- and third-order moduli. At third order, no new coupling arises; the modes interact through stiffness corrections involving the fourth-order modulus, which the dislocations further correct mode by mode.
tldr: The paper analyzes helical shear deformation of a thick-walled tube made of an incompressible, isotropic hyper-anelastic solid containing a radially symmetric distribution of axial screw dislocations, using the Bilby-Kröner-Lee decomposition.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how distributed axial screw dislocations (encoded via a Weitzenböck material manifold) modify the nonlinear elastic and weakly nonlinear shear response of a hyper-anelastic tube.
method: Equilibrium is reduced to an algebraic system for the azimuthal and axial shear strains, with exact solutions for neo-Hookean, Fung-Demiray, Gent, Knowles, and Mooney-Rivlin materials, numerical solutions for Gent-Gent materials, and a third-order weakly nonlinear expansion in tractions and dislocation strength.
result: Dislocations stiffen the tube when the strain energy stiffens with the first invariant, chirally couple the two shear modes when it depends on the second invariant, and can cap dislocation strength (Gent, Gent-Gent) or contract the admissible traction region (Knowles with n < 1/2).
conclusion: Chiral mode coupling first enters at second order in the applied tractions and dislocation strength, making every dislocated material couple modes as the Mooney-Rivlin solid at that order; third-order interactions involve stiffness corrections from the fourth-order modulus.

title: First-order Optimization Methods With Generalized Smoothness For Low-rank Matrix Factorization
authors: F. S. Stonyakin A. V. Bidanets
abstract: ArXiv:2610.19059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies several first-order methods for low-rank matrix minimization in the Burer--Monteiro form, where the target matrix is represented as the product of a nonnegative factor matrix and its transpose. Such a factorization destroys convexity of the objective function and global Lipschitz continuity of the gradient. We prove that for a quadratic objective function that is strongly convex only on the subspace of symmetric matrices, the Burer-Monteiro factorized objective possesses generalized smoothness with a fractional exponent 2/3. For a quadratic objective, the generalized smoothness property requires positive definiteness of the operator A only on the subspace of symmetric matrices, which relaxes the assumptions of Dragomir et al. On this basis, three methods are proposed: an adaptive gradient descent method with Armijo backtracking; an unconstrained SafeAdam method combining the Adam direction with a descent-angle certificate and a fallback to the normalized gradient; and a certified projected version for the nonnegativity constraint. Global convergence and explicit convergence rates for the proposed methods have been proved. The obtained convergence rate is better than the convergence rate of ordinary unaccelerated gradient descent in the case of a sufficiently large gradient. In the small-gradient regime, the convergence guarantee is of square-root type, and the corresponding complexity scales as the inverse square of the desired accuracy. In the large-gradient regime, the convergence guarantee is of three-quarters type, and the corresponding complexity is proportional to the inverse of the accuracy raised to the power of 4/3. Experiments on SymNMF using the TDT2, Reuters and CBCL datasets, which are standard benchmarks for document and image clustering, show that the methods match or outperform Dyn-NoLips without tuning the relative-smoothness kernel parameters.
tldr: This paper develops first-order optimization methods with generalized smoothness guarantees for Burer–Monteiro low-rank matrix factorization, applied to symmetric nonnegative matrix factorization benchmarks.
motivation: Burer–Monteiro factorization destroys convexity and standard gradient Lipschitz continuity, so classical first-order convergence theory does not apply; the authors seek methods with provable rates under weaker generalized-smoothness assumptions.
method: They prove the factorized quadratic objective satisfies generalized smoothness with fractional exponent 2/3 when the operator is positive definite only on symmetric matrices, then propose adaptive gradient descent with Armijo backtracking, an unconstrained SafeAdam with descent-angle certification, and a certified projected variant for nonnegativity.
result: Global convergence and explicit rates are established: square-root type convergence with complexity scaling as inverse squared accuracy in the small-gradient regime, and three-quarters type with complexity scaling as accuracy to the power -4/3 in the large-gradient regime, outperforming plain gradient descent and matching or beating Dyn-NoLips on SymNMF tasks (TDT2, Reuters, CBCL).
conclusion: The work relaxes smoothness assumptions for low-rank factorization and yields practical certified algorithms, but is purely a classical optimization contribution with no quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, or hybrid-system content.
